READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND TO MATTHEW 10:1-42

  1. The newly chosen disciples are sent out on a mission trip which was foreshadowed in Matt. 9:37-38. Jesus also sent, at a later time, a larger group of seventy disciples (cf. Luke 10:1ff).

  2. This passage is paralleled in Mark 3:14-16; 6:7-13; and Luke 9:1-6. There may have been several of these kinds of mission trips.

  3. Jesus' message to the Twelve has three divisions marked off by the recurrent phrase "Truly, I say to you," Matt. 10:15,23,42.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Matthew 10:2 "the names of the twelve apostles"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:2 "the names of the twelve apostles" The term " apostle" (see note at Matt. 10:5) is used only in Matthew (here) and Mark (3:14) in connection with the list of the apostles' names, also once more in Mark 6:30. It is much more common in Luke and Acts.

  1. Luke 6:13; 9:10; 11:49; 17:5; 22:14; 24:10
  2. Acts
    1. the Twelve, Acts 1:2,26; 2:37,42,43; 4:33,35,36,37; 5:2,12,18,29,40; 6:6; 8:1,14,18; 9:27; 11:1; 15:2,4,6,22,23; 16:4
    2. other apostles (later use of the term)
      (1) Paul, Acts 14:4,14 (equal authority with the Twelve)
      (2) Barnabas Acts 14:14 (lesser authority)

The lists of the Apostles are found in Mark 3:16-19, Luke 6:12-16, and Acts 1:13-14. The names and order change slightly. However, they are always in three groups of four. Peter is always first and Judas Iscariot is always last. The groupings stay the same. These groupings were possibly a rotating system whereby certain disciples could go home for short periods to check on their families.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTLES (send)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHART OF APOSTLES' NAMES

entries.title: Matthew 10:3 "Bartholomew"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:3 "Bartholomew" He was also called Nathaniel (cf. John. 1:45-51).

▣ "Matthew" He was also called Levi (cf. Mark 2:14; Luke 5:27).

▣ "Thaddeus" He was also called Judas, the son or brother of James (cf. Luke 6:16; Acts 1:13) or Lebbaeus (Greek MSS C2, L, and W).

10:4
NASB, NJB, Peshitta, REB, NET  "Simon the Zealot"
NKJV  "Simon the Canaanite"
NRSV  "Simon the Canaanean"
TEV  "Simon the Patriot"

He was also called "the Cananean," which could refer to one from Cana (cf. Mark 3:18). However, the Greek reflects an Aramaic and Hebrew term "zealous." He may have been a Jewish patriot and separatist (cf. Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13). For Matthew and Simon to be in the same group shows the radical change that Jesus accomplished in these men's lives.

▣ "Iscariot" This term can mean a man from a city in Judah, Kerioth (from the Hebrew), or an assassin's knife (from the Greek). If he was from Judah, he was the only Apostle from the south.

For more detailed information see Bruce M. Metzger, A Textual Commentary On the Greek New Testament, pp. 26-27.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISCARIOT (the name)

▣ "the one who betrayed him" There is an interesting book that attempts to interpret Judas in a new, a more positive way, Judas, Betrayer or Friend of Jesus? by William Klassen, published by Fortress Press, 1996. However, to do so it completely ignores John's Gospel.

entries.title: Matthew 10:5 "sent"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:5 "sent" This was from the same Greek root as "apostle" (apostello, used in the LXX for God sending the prophets to speak for Him), which came to mean "sent one" within rabbinical circles with the implication of official authority. Mark 6:7 tells us Jesus sent the Apostles out in pairs.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEND

▣ "do not go in the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter any city of the Samaritans" This is probably the source of Paul's "Jew first and also the Greeks" (cf. Rom 1:16). This was not exclusivism, but limiting His emphasis so as to give Abraham's descendants every chance to respond. They knew the Hebrew Bible and should have recognized Him. Jesus was sent to inform and call to repentance the house of Israel. When they, primarily the leadership, would not; Jesus revealed the judgment that would fall on them (i.e., the Jewish Wars, A.D. 66-70).

The Jews hated the Samaritans because they were considered half-breeds. This referred to the Assyrian exile of the Northern Ten Tribes of Israel in 722 B.C. Thousands of Jews were deported to Media and thousands of Gentiles were imported to take their place in Israel. Over the years an amalgamation of religion and social customs had occurred (cf. Ezra and Neh.). At this early stage of Jesus' ministry the inclusion of either of these groups would have negatively affected His ability to reach Jews!

entries.title: Matthew 10:6 "the lost sheep"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:6 "the lost sheep" This was an unusual combination of terms; "sheep" often referred to God's people (cf. Psalm 23; John. 10), while "lost" implied their spiritual helplessness and vulnerability (cf. Matt. 9:36), especially if there is no shepherd (cf. Num. 27:17; 1 Kgs. 22:17; Ps. 119:176; Isa. 53:6; Zech. 13:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

▣ "of the house of Israel" This was an idiomatic way of referring to the descendants of the Patriarchs. They are also known as

  1. the house of Jacob (i.e., Luke 1:33, cf. Matt. 15:24; Acts 2:36; Heb. 8:8)
  2. the house of Judah (i.e., Heb. 8:8)
  3. children of Abraham (i.e., Matt. 3:9; John 8:33,39)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

entries.title: Matthew 10:7 "as you go"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:7 "as you go" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE used as an IMPERATIVE (cf. Matt. 28:19, where the VERBAL is an AORIST PASSIVE PARTICIPLE used as an IMPERATIVE).

▣ "preach" This was a PRESENT IMPERATIVE. This is a foreshadowing of the mission trips of the Twelve and seventy. Jesus' words here do not include the Gentile mission.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

▣ "kingdom. . .is at hand" This was to be the content that they were to preach (cf. Matt. 3:2; 4:17; Mark 1:15; Luke 10:9,11; 11:20; 21:31). The kingdom is the reign of God in human's hearts now which will one day be consummated over all the earth (cf. Matt. 6:10). Although the disciples did not understand it yet (i.e., Luke 24:16,31), it began with the Incarnation of Christ (the Messiah) and will be consummated at the Second Coming of Christ. Initially Jesus and the disciples preached a message similar to John the Baptist's message (i.e., Matt. 3:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

entries.title: Matthew 10:8 "heal. . .raise. . .cleanse. . .cast out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:8 "heal. . .raise. . .cleanse. . .cast out" These are all PRESENT IMPERATIVES (cf. Matt. 10:1). They went and ministered as Jesus ministered. His power and authority were flowing through them. These signs confirmed their message about Him.

The Greek manuscripts contain several variations of the phrase "raise the dead." This may be because

  1. biblical records are lacking that the twelve Apostles did this
  2. it is imagery for the spiritually dead
  3. Matthew used the other three VERBS often without mentioning "raising the dead"
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB, NJB  "raise the dead"
Peshitta    omit
TEV  "bring the dead back to life"

It is missing in the uncial MSS C3, L, X, Y and about 150 later minuscule MSS, as well as several translations (i.e., Syriac, Coptic, Armenean, Ethiopian, and Georgian). It was also not mentioned here by Eusebius or Basil. The UBS4 committee thought it was omited by accident.

See Bruce Metzger, A Textual Commentary On the Greek New Testament, pp. 27-28. The phrase is included in the uncial MSS א, B, C, D, N, and many versions.

▣ "lepers" In the OT the disease of leprosy (cf. Leviticus 13-14) was a sign of God's disfavor (cf. 2 Chr. 26:16-23). This term in the OT included many more issues than the modern term, leprosy.

▣ "cast out demons" Jesus' power is greater than Satan and the demonic (cf. 1 John. 4:4). The demons are designated by the terms "spirits," (cf. Matt. 8:16) and "unclean spirits," (cf. Matt. 10:1). The origin of demons is not disclosed in Scripture. The rabbis attribute the origin of evil in the world to Genesis 6 (Paul says it was Genesis 3, cf. Rom. 5:12-21). They assert that the "sons of God" mentioned in Genesis 6 became disembodied at their death by the flood of Noah and became the demons of the NT period seeking another body (cf. 1 Enoch).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EXORCISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: "the sons of God" in Genesis 6

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (pneuma) IN THE NT, C.

▣ "freely you received, freely give" This is not a passage against salaries for missionaries, but rather encouraging believers to trust in God while doing Kingdom work in

  1. His power
  2. His provisions
  3. His purposes to be accomplished

These verses are not universal principles, but guidelines for this particular mission trip (cf. Luke 22:35-36). They are the practical application of Matt. 6:25-34 to the present situation.

entries.title: Matthew 10:9 "your money belts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:9 "your money belts" This was how first century Jews carried their coinage.

entries.title: Matthew 10:10 "bag"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:10 "bag" This kind of bag functioned as a suitcase. The disciples were not to carry with them every thing they might need, but trust God's daily provision.

▣ "or even two coats, or sandals, or a staff" Comparisons with Mark 6:8-9 have caused great controversy. The theories are

  1. "staff" could be used in two different senses: a walking stick or a defensive club
  2. the two shirts of Matt. 10:10 imply "do not take extras of these items"
  3. Luke 22:35-36 shows one harmonization

The Gospels were not written for us to compare the details. The key to this text is that believers are to trust in God for His provisions; rely on His resources!

▣ "for the worker is worthy of his support" Jesus is probably alluding to the truth of Deut. 25:4 (cf. 1 Cor. 9:6-7,14; 1 Tim. 5:18), which goes back to Deut. 24:14-15 (cf. Lev. 19:13). Gospel preachers are to be supported by their hearers! The NT guidelines for giving are not OT tithing, but voluntary, sacrificial, joyful, according to the ability (cf. 2 Corinthians 8-9; see full notes online).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING

10:11
NASB  "inquire who is worthy in it; and stay at this house until you
  leave that city"
NKJV  "inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there till you go out"
NRSV  "find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave"
TEV  "Go in and look for someone who is willing to welcome you,
  and stay with him untill you leave that place"
NJB  "Seek out someone worthy and stay with him until you leave"
Peshitta  "Ask who is trustworthy in it, and remain there until you leave"

When they came to a village

  1. they were to seek out a godly home which desired the blessing of their presence and were open to the gospel
  2. they were not to move again and again seeking better accommodations

It is possible that the godly home would be one of the first that responded to their preaching.

entries.title: Matthew 10:12 "give it your greeting"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:12 "give it your greeting" This referred to the traditional Jewish blessing of peace, shalom.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom)

entries.title: Matthew 10:13 "if. . .if"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:13 "if. . .if" There are two THIRD CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCES which meant potential future action.

entries.title: Matthew 10:14 "shake the dust off your feet"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:14 "shake the dust off your feet" This was a Jewish symbol of rejection (cf. Acts 13:51; 18:6).

entries.title: Matthew 10:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:15 This is one passage that implies degrees of judgment based on the amount of light that has been rejected (cf. Matt. 11:22-24). Also notice the same book which reveals God's matchless love also reveals God's wrath and judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE UNPARDONABLE SIN

▣ "Truly" See SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN.

entries.title: Matthew 10:16 "I send you out as sheep"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:16 "I send you out as sheep" "Sheep" was imagery for the new faith community which was fragile, helpless, and in need of constant care and protection (see Luke 10:3 and John. 10). This the first of four images from the animal kingdom that characterize humanity.

▣ "in the midst of wolves" Wolves represented those who prey on the new community of faith (cf. Matt. 7:15-27; Luke 10:3; John. 10:12; Acts 20:29; 2 Peter 2).

▣ "shrewd as serpents and innocent as doves" Believers must be wise but innocent (cf. Rom. 16:19). They were to avoid conflict when possible, but remain bold proclaimers of the gospel.

entries.title: Matthew 10:17 "But beware of men"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:17 "But beware of men" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE (cf. Matt. 7:15; 16:6,11). Even with the dawn of the new age (Romans 5-6), the old age remains (Romans 7)! This is the tension of " the already" and the "not yet" of the overlapping (i.e., two comings of Christ) of the two ages.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

▣"the courts" This referred to local Jewish synagogue courts (cf. Matt. 23:34). It is interesting to note that some of Mark's eschatological discourse (cf. Mark 13:9-13) of Jesus is repeated here instead of Matthew 24. Therefore, this mission assignment of the Disciples takes on A.D. 70 implications (as does Matt. 10:23).

▣ "scourge" This referred to Jewish flogging (cf. Deut. 25:3), which consisted of one less than forty lashes, one-third on the front of the body and two-thirds on the back (cf. 2 Cor. 11:24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SCOURGED

▣ "in their synagogues" See parallel at Matt. 23:34. This was the local place of worship, education, and welfare relief. Jesus is speaking to a first century Palestinian context.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYNAGOGUE

entries.title: Matthew 10:18 "you will even be brought before governors and kings"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:18 "you will even be brought before governors and kings" This referred to the future universal spread of the gospel (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8). It is important that the narrow exclusiveness of Matt. 10:5 be balanced by this verse. Gordon Fee (How to Read the Bible For All Its Worth, p. 133) makes the assertion that Matt. 10:5-12 relates to the sending out of the Twelve new apostles, but Matt. 10:10-20 has instructions for a much later time (i.e., governors, kings, Gentiles) because at first Jesus came only to the lost sheep of Israel. This illustrates how the Gospel writers "selected, rearranged, and adapted" Jesus' teachings to meet the needs of the early church.

Another example of this is Matt. 10:23 "until the Son of Man comes," which obviously refers to A.D. 70.

▣ "governors and kings" If this refers to (1) Jesus' day, then Pontius Pilate or (2) Paul's mission activities then

  1. "governors" could be the Roman governors of Felix (Acts 23:24) or Festus (Acts 24:27)
  2. "kings" could be Agrippa I (Acts 12:1) or Agrippa II (Acts 25:13)

They basically stand for governmental authority of Palestine or the Roman Empire.

entries.title: Matthew 10:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:19 This speaks of special illumination and grace during Jewish and later Roman persecution (cf. Mark 13:11; Luke 21:12). This is not a proof-text for preachers and teachers not studying before proclaiming! This Matt. 10:19 and 26 are AORIST SUBJUNCTIVES with the NEGATIVE PARTICLE which meant never start an action. Matthew 10:28 and 31, which also deal with fear, are PRESENT IMPERATIVES with the NEGATIVE PARTICLE which usually meant stop an act in process.

▣ "hour" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HOUR

entries.title: Matthew 10:20 "it is the Spirit of your Father"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:20 "it is the Spirit of your Father" Here the Holy Spirit is linked to the Father (cf. Rom. 8:11,14). In Rom. 8:9; 2 Cor. 3:17; Gal. 4:6; and 1 Pet. 1:11 the Spirit is linked to the Son. There is a fluidity between the persons of the Trinity. They all participate in the acts of redemption.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (pneuma) in the NT

entries.title: Matthew 10:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:21 This speaks of the radical commitment necessary for discipleship which supersedes even family love and often caused confrontation within families (cf. Matt. 10:34-38).

entries.title: Matthew 10:22 "you will be hated by all because of My name"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:22 "you will be hated by all because of My name" Persecution was expected for disciples of Jesus (cf. Matt. 5:10-12; John 15:18-21; 16:1-3; 17:14; Acts 14:22; Rom. 5:3-4; 8:17; 2 Cor. 4:16-18; 6:3-10; 11:23-30; Phil. 1:29; 1 Thess. 3:3; 2 Tim. 3:12; James 1:2-4; and all of 1 Peter.

In this context it primarily refers to Jewish opposition and persecution of the belief that Jesus of Nazareth was the promised Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO CHRISTIANS SUFFER?

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Name of the Lord (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "it is the one who has endured to the end who will be saved" The doctrine of the "perseverance" is as biblical as "the security of the believers!" (cf. Matt. 24:13; Gal. 6:9; Rev. 2:7,11,17,26; 3:5,12; 21:7). We must affirm both truths, even though they cause doctrinal tension! Doctrines are given in tension-filled relationship to other doctrines, not isolated truths. The best illustration is that biblical truth is revealed as constellations of stars, not as single stars. We must focus on the patterns of the whole of biblical revelation.

"End" (telos) refers to the end of the Jewish age (cf. Matt. 24:6,13,14), therefore, it relates to the destruction of the temple in Jerusalem.

"Saved" can be understood in its OT sense of physical deliverance or its NT sense of spiritual salvation. But here, I think it refers to Jesus' warnings to Jewish believers related to Titus' siege of Jerusalem (cf. Matt. 24:15-28; Mark 13:14-23; Luke 21:20-24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ASSURANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

entries.title: Matthew 10:23 "But, whenever they persecute you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:23 "But, whenever they persecute you" This is missing in Luke, but has a parallel in Mark 9:1. Jewish believers are persecuted because of their relationship with Jesus. They affirm that He is the promised Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO CHRISTIANS SUFFER?

▣ "flee to the next" Believers must avoid conflict and confrontation when possible. Evangelism must be the constant goal!

▣ "Truly" See SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN.

▣ "you will not finish going through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes" This could have been initially understood as

  1. Jesus will rejoin the Twelve after their mission
  2. Jesus asserts His authority in Jerusalem
  3. inauguration of the church (i.e., Pentecost)
  4. Jesus fulfilling His promises to them (i.e., upper room event of John 20:19-23)
  5. the judgment on Jerusalem in A.D. 70 (NASB Study Bible, p. 1382)
  6. Jesus' Second Coming in power as Judge (i.e., Dan. 7:13-14), inaugurating the eternal kingdom

I have come to believe that #5 is demanded by all the Synoptic Gospels. This eschatological position is known as Partial Preterism. For a detailed explanation of this position see

  1. John Bray, Matthew 24 Fulfilled
  2. Kenneth Gentry
    1. Before Jerusalem Fell
    2. The Beast of Revelation
    3. The Apocalypse of John: A Preterist Commentary of the Book of Revelation
  3. Four Views on the Book of Revelation, several authors, note pp. 39-92
  4. Steve Gregg
    1. Revelation: Four views, Revised and Expanded
    2. Why Not Full-Preterism? A Partial-Preterist Response to a Novel Theological Innovation
    3. Many thought provoking YouTube videos on biblical issues and controversies; his website is www.thenarrowpath.com; I highly recommend this brother's Bible study and lectures on contemporary controversies.  YouTube Lecture - 1:34:57
  5. Gary DeMar
    1. Last Days Madness: Obsession of the Modern Church
    2. End Time Fiction" A Biblical Consideration of Left Behind Theology
  6. Bruce Gore, YouTube video, "The Apocalypse in Space and Time" (10 lectures with detailed historical and Early Church Father quotes; very detailed and interesting)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANY-MOMENT RETURN OF JESUS vs. THE NOT YET (NT paradox)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOON RETURN

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

entries.title: Matthew 10:25 "If"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:25 "If" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed to be true from the author's perspective or for his literary purposes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII.

▣ "Beelzebul" This was a compound term from Ba'al and Zebub. This was the local Ba'al of Ekron (cf. 2 Kgs. 1:16). The Jews changed the names of pagan rulers and pagan gods by changing the vowels, to make fun of them. The term can be translated as

  1. "Lord of the house"
  2. "Lord of the flies"
  3. "Lord of the dung"

The second term was often spelled Zebul, the chief demon in Jewish folklore (cf. Matt. 12:24; Luke 11:15). This explains why NASB and NRSV have Beelzebul, while NKJV and NIV have Beelzebub.

This OT title is mentioned because the Jewish leaders tried to explain Jesus' power and miracles by Him being led by Satan or demon possessed (cf. Matt. 9:32-34; 12:22-29; Luke 11:14-15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BEELZEBUL

entries.title: Matthew 10:26 "do not fear them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:26 "do not fear them" This is a negative AORIST PASSIVE (deponent) SUBJUNCTIVE like Matt. 10:19 functioning as an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE like Matt. 10:28 and 31. This construction meant "do not even start an action." This verse states that the motives and purposes of the human hearts, both positive and negative, will be known on Judgment Day.

It is difficult to relate the truth of this verse with the biblical promises that when God forgives, God forgets (cf. Ps. 103:11-14; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Micah 7:19). Possibly unconfessed (believers, cf. 1 John 1:7-9) sin or unforgiven (unbelievers) sin is being referred to. I so rejoice in the "forgetfulness of God"! Jesus' blood cleanses from all sin (cf. Hebrew 9)!

Believers are not to fear humans, but respect/fear God (cf. Matt. 10:28; Heb. 10:31).

Overall I think this verse refers to the motives and actions of

  1. unworthy houses, Matt. 10:13
  2. wolves, Matt. 10:16
  3. evil men, Matt. 10:17
  4. governors and kings, Matt. 10:18
  5. brother, Matt. 10:21
  6. child, Matt. 10:21
  7. "they" of Matt. 10:23
  8. "them" of Matt. 10:26
  9. "those" of Matt. 10:28

entries.title: Matthew 10:27 "housetops"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:27 "housetops" The flat rooftops common in Palestine were places of social activity; therefore, what was told would become public knowledge. Jesus wants His message known by all mankind!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Matthew 10:28 "Do not fear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:28 "Do not fear" See notes at Matt. 10:26.

▣ "to destroy" I have recently become aware of the three different views of the early church related to "Hell." Each view has some verses that need to be exegeted. It seems the church through the centuries has allowed some differing opinions on the issue of the eternal state of unbelievers. I recommend two YouTube videos on this subject to show the different views.

  1. Edward Fudge ‒ "The Fire That Consumes"  YouTube One Hour Lecture
  2. Steve Gregg ‒ "Hell ‒ Three Christian Views"  YouTube Lecture - 1:34:57

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESTRUCTION (apollumi)

▣ "soul and body" This verse does not refer to a sharp dichotomy between body, soul, and spirit, but is an expression of the possibility of physical death, but not eternal death for believers (cf. 2 Cor. 5:6,8). The Hebrew view is that humans are a soul (cf. Gen. 2:7). However, the time between death and resurrection seems to point toward a temporary disembodied period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BODY AND SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "in hell" This was the Hebrew term "Gehenna." It was a compound of "valley" and "(sons of) Hinnom." This was a valley outside Jerusalem where a Canaanite fertility and fire god (cf. Lev. 18:21) was worshiped by sacrificing children (called molech). The Jews turned it into the garbage dump for Jerusalem. Jesus' imagery of eternal punishment was taken from this burning, stinking, worm-infested dump.

There is a judgment day coming where humans must give an account to God on their stewardship of the gift of life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, II. D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

entries.title: Matthew 10:29-30 "sparrows. . .hairs"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:29-30 "sparrows. . .hairs" God cares and knows about every aspect of believers' lives (cf. Luke 12:6; 21:18; 1 Pet. 5:7). This is a wonderful promise for individuals (not just corporate) concern.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

▣ "a cent" This is literally "assarion," which was a Roman copper coin. One assarion could buy several sparrows.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COINS USED IN PALESTINE IN JESUS' DAY

entries.title: Matthew 10:31 "So do not fear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:31 "So do not fear" See notes at Matt. 10:19 and 26.

entries.title: Matthew 10:32 "everyone"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:32 "everyone" I love the words, "everyone," "as many as," "whosoever," "all who"!

▣ "who confesses Me before men" This meant "publicly acknowledge" Jesus as God's Messiah (cf. Mark 8:38; Luke 12:8-9). Matthew 10:32 and 33 are contrasting parallel statements. Christianity is a God-offered unconditional covenant that must be personally, publicly received, obeyed and maintained (i.e., a conditional covenant).

SPECIAL TOPIC: What Does It Mean To "Receive," "Believe," "Confess/Profess," and "Call Upon?"

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESSION/PROFESSION

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "My Father in heaven" There are several different PRONOUNS used in connection with Father.

  1. your – Matt. 5:16,45; 6:1; 7:11
  2. our – Matt. 6:9
  3. My – Matt. 7:21; 10:32,33; 12:50

I think Matt. 12:50 is crucial, one who does the Father's will, as Jesus does, is part of the family. One who refuses is not part of the family. It must have been particularly irritating to the Jewish leaders of Jesus' day to hear Him, an unofficial rabbi and Galilean upstate, to use "Father" to refer to YHWH, the Holy One of Israel. Even more so to allow the outcast to be included in God's family while they are excluded (cf. Matt. 8:11-12)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

entries.title: Matthew 10:33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:33 The ANTONYM of "confess" (homologeō, cf. Matt. 10:32 [twice]) is "deny" (arneomai, cf. Matt. 10:33 [twice]; Matt. 26:70,72 [aparneomai in Matt. 26:35,75]).

This is a shocking verse, as is 2 Tim. 2:12. It must be remembered that public acknowledgment in word (cf. Rom. 10:9-13) and deed (cf. Matt. 13:1-23; 25:36-46) is crucial. The decisions made now affect eternity (cf. Matt. 25:46).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESSION/PROFESSION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

entries.title: Matthew 10:34 "Do not think"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:34 "Do not think" According to the Analytical Greek New Testament by Barbara and Timothy Friberg, this VERB is an AORIST ACTIVE SUBJUNCTIVE used as an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE.

Jesus was probably speaking these words against the backdrop of the Jewish expectations concerning the Messiah, who was called the "Prince of Peace" (cf. Isa. 9:6). The Jews expected the Messiah to usher in a military order and a nationalistic peace on the Jews' behalf (cf. Luke 12:49-53). They expected a divinely empowered Judge, as in the early days of Israel's history.

▣ "peace" This term's etymology was "to bring together that which was broken" (cf. John. 14:24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (NT)

▣ "I did not come to bring peace, but a sword" Jesus did not come to bring war or strife, but the fact that He has come forces humans to make a radical decision between "followship" or rejection (cf. John. 3:17; Luke 12:51-53).

entries.title: Matthew 10:35 "for I came to set a man against his father"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:35 "for I came to set a man against his father" See Matt. 10:21. The parallel in Luke 14:26 has the Hebrew idiom, "hate father," which was an idiom of comparison. We must recognize this as a Hebrew idiom instead of interpreting it literally (cf. Gen. 29:31, 33; Deuteronomy. 15; Mal. 1:2-3; John. 12:25). This speaks of a radical priority commitment to Jesus which supercedes all earthly ties.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HATE

entries.title: Matthew 10:35-36
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:35-36 This is a quote from Micah 7:6. This passage was often quoted in eschatological settings (cf. Mark 13:12 and Luke 12:53).

entries.title: Matthew 10:36 "a man's enemies will be the members of his household"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:36 "a man's enemies will be the members of his household" A good example of this type of familial pressure can be seen in

  1. Jesus' own family where most of His siblings did not believe or support Him until after His resurrection
  2. Peter's response to Jesus' claim to Messiahship (cf. Matt. 16:22)
  3. this kind of painful experience still occurs in cultures where Christianity is rejected

entries.title: Matthew 10:37 "He who loves. . .more than Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:37 "He who loves. . .more than Me" The key here is radical priority commitment (cf. Luke 14:26). Discipleship, unlike decision, is a life-long commitment of followship and obedience! The Great Commission (cf. Matt. 28:19-20) is a call to radical discipleship, not a fleeting decision that does not impact all of one's life (i.e., 2 Cor. 5:14-17)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES

▣ "is not worthy of Me" See notes at Luke 9:62.

entries.title: Matthew 10:38 "take his cross and follow after Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:38 "take his cross and follow after Me" This is graphic imagery summonsing believers to total commitment to Christ for life. Jesus is demanding that possible followers count the cost (cf. Luke 14:25-35). Discipleship is more than an initial decision, no matter how emotional or sincere. It is a complete reorientation of one's entire life and thought!

The cross was a Phoenician method of execution that was taken over by the Romans and developed into an ordeal involving several days of excruciating pain before death. Its purpose was to discourage non-Romans from criminal activity. There was a historical precedent of its use in Palestine:

  1. Antiochus IV "Epiphanes" crucified eight hundred Pharisees
  2. Varus, a Roman general, put down a revolt and crucified two thousand Jews along the highways of Palestine (cf. Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews 17:10:10)
  3. Herod planned on crucifying many Pharisees at his death so that people would grieve

This imagery does not refer to some particular problem in your life. It refers to death — death to self (cf. 2 Cor. 5:14-15; Gal. 2:20; 1 John. 3:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CRUCIFIXION

entries.title: Matthew 10:39 "life. . .life"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:39 "life. . .life" This was the Greek term psuche. This term was often synonymous with "spirit" [pneuma]. In this context, however, it seems to refer to an individual person or self. This statement involved a radical crucifixion of self interest in light of Jesus' interest (cf. Matt. 10:39; 16:25; Mark 8:35; Luke 9:24; 17:33; John. 12:25). Salvation involves far more than an initial decision or prayer. It demands one's all (possessions, family, reputation, time, and energy)! Nothing less will do!

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (pneuma) IN THE NT

▣ "lose" See SPECIAL TOPIC: DESTRUCTION (apollumi).

entries.title: Matthew 10:40,41 "He who receives you receives Me. . .a prophet. . .a righteous man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:40,41 "He who receives you receives Me. . .a prophet. . .a righteous man" The context seems to imply that Jesus is referred to personally by all these terms.

  1. The term "prophet" alludes to Deut. 18:15 and 18.
  2. The term "righteous man" equals "the Righteous One" of Acts 7:52 and possibly the Dead Sea Scrolls phrase "teacher of righteousness."

Jesus' radical new message was directed to those who would trust Him and His words. One must first repent and receive Him as their savior and Lord. In so doing they become identified with the new spiritual kingdom of God. The disciple represents Jesus Himself and His message, therefore, whoever receives them and their message, receives Jesus. To receive Jesus is to receive the Father (cf. John 8:19; 16:3; 17:3; 1 John 2:23; 4:15; 5:1,10-12; 2 John 9). One cannot know or fellowship with the Father except through the Son (cf. John 14:6-7,8-11; 1 John 5:10-12).

▣ "receives" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RECEIVE

▣ "Him who sent Me" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SEND (apostellō)

entries.title: Matthew 10:42 "gives to one of these little ones"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:42 "gives to one of these little ones" Loving help by one Christian should be given to another simply because they are both related to Jesus Christ. "Little ones" are not children, but new believers (cf. Matt. 18:6).

▣ "Truly" See SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN.

▣ "reward" The Bible is replete with statements concerning the Christian's reward. These rewards are based on the Spirit's activity in believers and their yieldedness to His activity. However, in the bountiful grace of God believers will be rewarded for their Christlike yieldedness and the effective operation of the Spirit working through their spiritual giftedness!

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did Jesus limit Himself mostly to the Jews? Can you list the exceptions?
  2. Why do Matthew, Mark, and Luke differ in their accounts of Jesus' life?
  3. Are there degrees of reward and punishment? Based on what?
  4. What is Matt. 10:23 referring to?
  5. Why is public acknowledgment of faith in Jesus so important?
  6. Why does Jesus cause such controversy?
  7. What does it mean to take up one's cross and follow Him?

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND TO MATTHEW: 11:1-30

  1. This chapter has often been described as unrelated stories, but the unifying factor seems to be the answer to the question, "Why was Jesus' ministry not more outwardly successful?"

  2. John the Baptist is a central character in this chapter (cf. John. 1:6-8, 19-36). He was the last of the Old Testament prophets (cf. Matt. 11:9).

  3. Isaiah lists several actions by which the Jews could recognize the Messiah, of whom John the Baptist was forerunner (i.e., Isa. 40:3; Mal. 3:1; 4:5b). These are the very actions of Jesus recorded in Matthew 8 and 9.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

11:1
NASB, REB  "giving instructions"
NRSV, NJB  "instructing"
NKJV, Peshitta  "commanding"

This is a PRESENT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE used often (i.e., similar phrase) to close sections of Matthew's presentation of Jesus' collected teachings (i.e., Matt. 7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1). Jesus passed on specific instructions to His followers on how to think, act, and live. The Bible is not optional truth but guidelines for daily life!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "to teach and preach in their cities" This is Jesus' main mission, to communicate the gospel, not to heal (cf. Matt. 4:23; 9:35). Healing was meant to confirm and validate the gospel, not to become the focus of His ministry. Healing was a way to

  1. show God's love
  2. show Jesus' power
  3. fulfill OT prophecy about the Messiah (cf. Matt. 11:5)
  4. show the validity of Jesus' new message about Himself

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

entries.title: Matthew 11:2 "John, while imprisoned"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:2 "John, while imprisoned" John the Baptist was imprisoned in Machaerus (Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews. 18.5.2), one of the fortresses of Herod Antipas. It is on the eastern side of the Dead Sea. Herod had imprisoned John for preaching against his marriage to Herod Phillip's former wife, Herodias. Antipas wooed her away from Phillip during a visit to Rome (cf. Josephus' Antiq. 18.5.2).

▣ "Christ" The term "Christ" equals the OT term Messiah which meant "an Anointed One." It was used in the sense of God's special call and equipping. In the OT, prophets, priests, and kings were anointed. Jesus fulfills all three of these anointed functions (cf. Heb. 1:1-3).

King Cyrus of the Persian Empire, who was an unbeliever, was even called God's anointed (cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:1), which shows the wider use of the term in the ANE.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Matthew 11:3 "Are You the Expected One, or shall we look for someone else"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:3 "Are You the Expected One, or shall we look for someone else" This was a Messianic title (cf. Ps. 118:26; alluded to often, Matt. 21:9; 23:39; Mark 11:9; Luke 13:35; 19:38; John 6:14; 11:27; 12:13; and Heb. 10:37).

In Luke 1:15 John was filled with the Spirit, but he still had doubts. Several theories explain John's doubting.

  1. John was discouraged because he was in prison
  2. John Calvin says that this was his way of referring his disciples to Jesus
  3. Jesus was not acting in the expected manner (i.e., as victorious military leader and Judge, cf. Matt. 3:7-12)

"Someone else" is the Greek term heteros which meant, in Classical Greek, "another of a different kind." John expected a message of judgment from the Messiah, instead Jesus offered salvation to all.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Matthew 11:4-5 "Jesus answered and said to them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:4-5 "Jesus answered and said to them" Matthew 11:5 is a quote from Isaiah. It is debated whether it was from Isa. 26:19; 29:18,19; 35:5-6; or 61:1. It does emphasize the ministry of the Messiah as a ministry of compassion and the healing of the poor and outcast.

entries.title: Matthew 11:5 "Gospel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:5 "Gospel" The NOUN form (euangelion, over 60 times in Paul's writings) is found in Matt. 4:23; 9:35; 24:14; and 26:13. The VERB form (euangelizumai) is found only here in Matthew (not in John). This word describes the contents of Jesus' message, "good news." It includes the "bad news" of the sin and separation of all humans from God (i.e., Rom. 1:18-3:20), but continues in the offer of forgiveness, restoration, and eternal salvation for all in faith in Christ (cf. Rom. 3:21-30). The good news of victory in the spiritual conflict (cf. Romans 7; Eph. 6:10-20)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

entries.title: Matthew 11:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:6 This was a gentle rebuke of John's lack of faith. The Bible depicts its characters in both positive and negative ways. This shows its credibility. It was not propaganda, but true historical people and their feelings and faults!

Matthew chose to record this because it gets back to the major theological issue — who is Jesus?

entries.title: Matthew 11:7 "A reed shaken by the wind"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:7 "A reed shaken by the wind" Notice the threefold parallelism, "what did you go out to see?" John was like Elijah; he fulfilled the predictions fo Mal. 3:1 and Isa. 40:3 (cf. Mark 1:2-3).

This may relate to

  1. John's doubt which had just been expressed publicly in his question (i.e., Matt. 11:3)
  2. John's steadfast character and moral courage in denouncing sin (i.e., the Pharisees' and Herod's)

entries.title: Matthew 11:9 "and one who is more than a prophet"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:9 "and one who is more than a prophet" John was not the first gospel preacher, but the last OT prophet predicted by Isaiah and Malachi. It is difficult to compare OT prophets with NT prophets. OT prophets wrote Scripture, but not NT prophets. Some of the Apostles, like Paul, claimed to be a prophet, but not all. What then is the purpose of the NT gift?

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

entries.title: Matthew 11:10 "this is the one about whom it is written"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:10 "this is the one about whom it is written" This is a quote from Mal. 3:1. It was a reference to a royal visit and the feverous preparation by local people which preceded it. Mark 1:2-3 is a composite quote from Mal. 3:1 and Isa. 40:3. This same concept is found in Isa. 57:14; 62:10.

Matthew collects the life and teachings of Jesus to convince Jews that He is the Messiah (the Coming One). This is done by quoting many OT texts. They are introduced in a variety of ways.

  1. a prophet is unnamed or alluded to
    1. the prophet, Matt. 1:22 (unnamed, Isa. 7:14)
    2. the prophet, Matt. 2:5 (unnamed, Micah 5:2
    3. the prophet, Matt. 13:35 (unnamed, Ps. 78:2)
    4. the prophet, Matt. 21:4 (unnamed, Isa. 62:11)
  2. a prophet is named
    1. Isaiah – Matt. 3:3; 4:14; 12:17; 13:14; 15:7
    2. Jeremiah – Matt. 2:18; 27:9
  3. it is written (perfect passive), Matt. 4:6,10; 11:10; 21:13; 26:24,31
  4. God said, Matt. 15:4; 22:31
  5. have you not read, Matt. 19:4; 21:16,42
  6. Moses said, Matt. 22:24
  7. David in the Spirit, Matt. 22:43

Jesus' birth, life, death, resurrection, and return were fulfillments of OT prophecy (cf. Matt. 26:54-56).

entries.title: Matthew 11:11 "Truly"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:11 "Truly" This is literally "amen," the Hebrew word for faith (cf. Hab. 2:4). Its original etymology meant "to be firm" or "to be sure." It was often used initially by Jesus to introduce a significant statement.

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

▣ "among those born of women" This verse is not a put down of John the Baptist, but an affirmation that he was the last of the OT prophets (cf. Matt. 13:16, 17). In a sense this was Jesus' way of affirming the significance of the new age (New Covenant, Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36), inaugurated by Himself.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

11:12
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent
  take it by force"
TEV  "the Kingdom of heaven has suffered violent attacks, and
  violent men try to seize it"
NJB  "The Kingdom of heaven has been subjected to violence
  and the violent are taking it by storm"
Peshitta  "the Kingdom of heaven has been administered by force,
  and only those in power control it"

There has been much discussion about what this verse meant and how it should be translated. The first phrase can be used

  1. in a positive sense, indicate that the kingdom of heaven is vigorously pressing forward
  2. in a negative sense, refer to the violent reaction of the Jewish leaders to both John's and Jesus' preaching

The second phrase seems to be a play on the word "vigorous" and was used of sinners eagerly grasping, or responding to, the gospel (cf. Luke 16:16). The Septuagint uses this verb in the sense of a "strong invitation" (cf. Gen. 33:11; Jdgs. 19:7). A good brief discussion is found in Hard Sayings of The Bible, pp.479-480.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

entries.title: Matthew 11:13 "for all the prophets and Law"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:13 "for all the prophets and Law" The Hebrew canon was divided into three sections, "the Law," "the Prophets," and "the Writings." This was the NT way of indicating the entire OT (cf. Luke 24:44). The OT pointed toward Jesus and the gospel (cf. Matt. 5:17-19,20-48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW CANON

entries.title: Matthew 11:13 "until John"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:13 "until John" This seems to imply that the Old Covenant comes to an end (cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3 and the book of Hebrews) with the preaching of John the Baptist, who was the last Old Covenant prophet. Something radically new has come in Jesus. John is His forerunner! The new age of the Spirit; the New Covenant; the promise of Gen. 3:15; 12:3 has come! The New Testament is about Jesus, not Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Matthew 11:14 "if"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:14 "if" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed to be true from the author's perspective or for his literary purposes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII

▣ "John himself is Elijah who was to come" This is implied in Luke 1:17. In John. 1:20-25, John denied that he was Elijah, but this was in the context of the specific questioning by the Pharisees. John was denying that he was Elijah reborn. Jesus asserted that John the Baptist fulfilled the prophecy of the return of Elijah before the Messiah from Mal. 3:1 and 4:5, (cf. Matt. 11:10).

This is one of several places where OT texts are corrected/reinterpreted by Jesus (i.e., Matt. 5:31-32). Jesus is the Father's ultimate revelation. He is Lord of Scripture. Through the years of my personal Bible study, my own culture, personal preferences, and denominational indoctrination have affected the way I read texts. Modern westerners are so unaccustomed to prophetic, apocalyptic and ANE imagery. Three books that have helped me in this area are:

  1. D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic
  2. Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth
  3. C. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible

entries.title: Matthew 11:15 "He who has ears to hear, let him hear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:15 "He who has ears to hear, let him hear" This idiom (PRESENT PARTICIPLE and PRESENT IMPERATIVE) refers to the fact that unless the Holy Spirit aids believers' insight they cannot understand spiritual truth (cf. Isa. 6:9-10; 50:5; Matt. 13:9,43; Mark 4:9,23; Luke 8:8; 14:35; very similar to Rev. 2:7,11,17,29; 3:6,13,22; 13:9). However, it also implies that the willingness of the individual to hear and respond is also necessary. Revelation involves a divine initiator (unconditional covenant) and a human hearer/responder (i.e., conditional covenant).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Matthew 11:16 "like children sitting in the market place"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:16 "like children sitting in the market place" This is paralleled in Luke 7:31-32. Even though John the Baptist came as an ascetic (i.e., a prophet from the desert, like Elijah), the Jews rejected him. Jesus came as one who readily associated with humans of all social levels and yet they rejected Him too. This either speaks of the fickleness of the Jewish leaders or shows their preconceived biases.

entries.title: Matthew 11:17 "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:17 "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance" This social approach referred to the way Jesus interacted with people (cf. Matt. 11:19). The flute could be used for dancing (Matt. 11:17a) at both a party or a funeral (Matt. 11:17b).

▣ "we sang a dirge, but you did not mourn" This somber approach referred to the ministry of John the Baptist (cf. Matt. 11:18).

entries.title: Matthew 11:18 "He has a demon"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:18 "He has a demon" This same charge is made against Jesus in Matt. 9:34 and 12:24 (cf. John. 7:20; 8:48-49,52; 10:20). This is the only text that accuses John of having a demon. The Jews could not deny the power of either John or Jesus, but claimed that their source of authority and power was the evil one. This, ultimately, is the unpardonable sin.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: UNPARDONABLE SIN

entries.title: Matthew 11:19 "The Son of Man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:19 "The Son of Man" This was Jesus' self-chosen title because it had no militaristic nor nationalistic implications. It combined the human and divine aspects of Christ's nature (cf. Ezek. 2:1; Ps. 8:4; Dan. 7:13). The combination of aspects became a crucial NT truth (cf. 1 John 4:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners" Jesus acted in a very unexpected way. He befriended the same people the religious leaders rejected (cf. Matt. 9:11; Luke 5:30; 7:34; 15:2). This fulfills the Messianic predictions of Isaiah.

Religious legalism and asceticism have been such a spiritual/theological struggle for the church that I would like to quote a brief section from New International Dictionary of New Testament Theology, vol. 1, p. 495.

"Viewed as a whole, however, asceticism in the sense of renunciation of possessions, sexual activity, and food-restrictions is not generally enjoined by the teaching of Jesus in the Gospels. This does not mean that renunciation by a particular person in a concrete situation is excluded (cf. the story of the rich young ruler, Matt. 19:21). It is only that from such passages (cf. Matt. 11:19; 9:14ff; Mk. 2:18f; Lk. 5:33ff.), one cannot deduce a basic attitude on the part of Jesus, just as one cannot deduce his will for the overall validity of an ascetic ethic. Renunciation is only demanded where something stands in the way of following Jesus."

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT FOOD LAWS

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: CELIBACY AND MARRIAGE

▣
NASB, NRSV  "Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds"
NKJV  "But wisdom is justified by her children"
TEV  "God's wisdom, however, is shown to be true by its results"
NJB, REB  "Yet wisdom has been proved right by her actions"
Peshitta  "And yet wisdom is justified by its works"

The mention of "wisdom" alludes to Proverbs 8, where it is personified. Jesus is that personification. An example of this imagery is seen in Matt. 12:42, where Jesus is greater than the wisdom of Solomon (also note He is greater than the temple, Matt. 12:6 and greater than Jonah, Matt. 12:41). Even Jesus' use of "yoke" in Matt. 11:29 may be a reference to wisdom teachings.

There is a Greek manuscript variation here. By her "deeds" is found in the ancient Greek uncial manuscripts א, B, and W, while "children" is found in the Corrector of Vaticanus B2, C, D, K, and L. "Children" is the parallel in Luke 7:35 and seems to be added here by scribes to make the passages agree. "Deeds" may refer to Matt. 11:2. The UBS4 gives "deeds" a "B" rating (almost certain). The same truth is expressed in the phrase "by their fruits you shall know them" (cf. Matt. 7:16,20; 12:33). This is true of Jesus and of all people. The acts of Jesus in Matthew 8-9 revealed to those who would see that He was the promised Messiah (cf. Isa. 29:18-19; 35:5-6; 61:1-2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS IS GREATER THAN

entries.title: Matthew 11:20-24 "He began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles were done"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:20-24 "He began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles were done" This showed the proverbial truth that to whom much is given, much is required (cf. Luke 12:48). The cities of Jesus' day are compared with the OT cities. They had seen His miracles and heard His teachings. Nineveh had repented at the preaching of Jonah, while Tyre, Sidon, Sodom, and Gomorrah did not, yet the Galilean cities of Jesus' day had much greater light by which to respond. Those who have greater light are more responsible!

Jesus' comments were introduced by "woe" (i.e., lament or funeral dirge, cf. Matt. 18:7; 23:13,15,16,23,25,27,29; 24:19; 26:24). This was one of the three usual literary forms by which the OT prophets communicated their messages.

  1. promise oracle
  2. court scene
  3. funeral dirge or lament

▣ "repent" Repentance is a turning from sin and self, the negative aspect of salvation, while faith is a turning to God in Christ, the positive aspect of salvation (cf. Mark 1:15; Acts 3:16, 19; 20:21). By combining the meanings of the Greek and Hebrew words, the meaning of repentance is a change of mind followed by a change of action. Repentance is more than feelings (cf. 2 Cor. 7:8-11). It must result in a lifestyle change. See complete note at Matt. 4:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (NT)

entries.title: Matthew 11:21,23 "if"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:21,23 "if" This is a SECOND CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is called "contrary to fact," a false statement is made to highlight the false premise drawn from it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII. C.

entries.title: Matthew 11:21 "Chorazin"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:21 "Chorazin" This shows our limited knowledge of the works of Jesus, for we have no Gospel record of Jesus' miracles in this town. We must remember that the Gospels are selected theological truths to reveal Jesus to selected audiences (i.e., Jews, Romans, Gentiles), and not western chronological, cause-and-effect histories (cf. John. 20:30-31). See Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 127-148.

▣ "Bethsaida" There were two Bethsaidas. One was somewhere close to Capernaum and one at the place where the Jordan River flowed into the Sea of Galilee.

▣ "if" This is a SECOND CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE , see note at Matt. 11:21.

▣ "Tyre and Sidon" Tyre and Sidon were OT types of sinful, prideful nations or mankind (like Edom and Babylon). The phrase found in Matt. 11:23 related this to Isa. 14:13-15 and Ezek. 28:12-16. In these verses the pride of the Kings of Babylon and Tyre were used as examples of the pride of Satan.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN, IV. B.

▣ "in sackcloth and ashes" In context this may refer to a sign of repentance (cf. Jonah 3:5-8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

entries.title: Matthew 11:22 "it will be more tolerable for. . ."
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:22 "it will be more tolerable for. . ." There are degrees of both reward and punishment based on the amount of light to which the hearers have been exposed and responded to (cf. Luke 12:47, 48; Matt. 10:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

▣ "in the day of judgment" In Matthew's Gospel, Jesus talks often about "Judgment Day" (cf. Matt. 7:22; 10:15; 11:22,24; 12:36). The endtime scene is clearly revealed in Matt. 25:31-46.

There are judgments in time, like the fall of Jerusalem and the temple (i.e., 586 B.C.; A.D. 70), but also a general judgment at the end of time (i.e., Revelation 20). All conscious creatures created by God will give an account of the gift of life!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE JUDGMENT SEAT OF CHRIST

entries.title: Matthew 11:23 "And you, Capernaum, will not be exalted to heaven, will you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:23 "And you, Capernaum, will not be exalted to heaven, will you" This grammatical construction expects a "no" answer. This may be an allusion to Isa. 14:13-14 and Ezek. 28:2,5-6,17, which magnifies the pride of the kings of Babylon and Tyre.

▣ "descend to Hades" This may be an allusion to Isa. 14:15 or Ezek. 26:20; 28:8; 31:14; 32:18,24. This referred to the realm of the dead (cf. Luke 16:23) in Hebrew Sheol. According to the rabbis, there was a righteous part, called Paradise and a wicked part, called Tartarus. This may be true. Jesus' words to one of the criminals crucified with Him in Luke 23:43 seem to imply a righteous part of Hades because Jesus did not return to heaven until Pentecost. At Jesus' resurrection He took the righteous part of Hades (Sheol) to be with Him. Therefore, Paul can now say in 2 Cor. 5:8b that to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord. Be careful not to combine the concepts of Hades and Gehenna. They are distinct in the New Testament.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, II. B.

▣ "if" This is a SECOND CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is called "contrary to fact" (as was Matt. 11:21). This should then be translated, "If the miracles had occurred in Sodom, which occurred in you (but they did not), then it would have remained to this day, (which it did not)."

entries.title: Matthew 11:24 "the land of Sodom"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:24 "the land of Sodom" The word "land" may be the Aramaic phrase for "the city." Modern archaeologists believe this OT city was located on the southern end of the Dead Sea under water.

entries.title: Matthew 11:25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:25 In Luke 10:21 these words of Jesus are spoken after the return of the mission of the seventy. Remember the Gospels are not necessarily in chronological order! See Gordon Fee and douglas Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 127-148.

▣ "I praise You" This compound term in this context can mean to make open avowal (cf. Matt. 3:6; Phil. 2:11), to praise, or to celebrate. This same Greek term translated the Hebrew term for "praise" in the Septuagint. The Aramaic possibly meant "openly agree."

▣ "Lord of heaven and earth" This is a Hebraic idiom for physical creation. This affirms God as creator of all things. Interestingly, John, John 1:3,10; Paul, 1 Cor. 8:6, Col. 1:16; and the author of Hebrews, Heb. 1:2; 2:10, assert that Jesus is the Father's agent in creation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "You have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent and have revealed them to infants" This is a Semitic idiom meaning the things that all humans, not just the religious or worldly elite, can know about God. It is still surprising that the Jewish religious leaders who knew the OT did not recognize Jesus and put their faith in Him (cf. Romans 9). Isaiah 50:5 must occur before the result of sin (Isa. 6:9-10) can be reversed!

"Infants" referred to new believers (cf. Matt. 18:6).

entries.title: Matthew 11:26 "for this was well-pleasing in Your sight"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:26 "for this was well-pleasing in Your sight" This is a Hebrew idiom for "it was God's will" (cf. Luke 10:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL (thelēma) OF GOD

entries.title: Matthew 11:27 "all things have been handed over to Me by My Father"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:27 "all things have been handed over to Me by My Father" This was a strong affirmation of Jesus' self-understanding and sense of the unique authority given very early in His ministry (cf. Matt. 28:18; Luke 2:49; John 3:35; 13:3; Eph. 1:20-22, Col. 1:16-19; 2:10, and 1 Pet. 3:22). Jesus makes such strong statements about Himself (i.e., John 10:1-18; 14:1-24). He cannot be a great teacher, a religious genius! He is either the incarnated Son of God or a lunatic or a liar! There is no middle ground here! The NT is true or Christianity is a lie (cf. 1 Cor. 15:12-19). You must decide!

This verse sounds like John's Gospel (cf. John 3:35; 10:15; 13:3; 17:2). Yet this same truth is repeated in Matt. 28:18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ "nor does anyone know the Father" The intensified term "know," used twice, meant full, complete, and personal knowledge (i.e., epiginoskō). No one knows the Father but the Son (cf. John. 1:18; 17:25; 1 John 5:1-12). How wonderful that He chooses to reveal the Father to believing humans.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

▣ "and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal Him" This is not a proof-text for Jesus choosing some and not choosing others. Matt. 11:28 shows that God, by choosing Christ, chose all humans (cf. John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2; 4:14). It also asserts that Jesus is the ultimate revelation of the invisible, eternal God (cf. Matt. 5:17-48; John 1:1,18; Col. 1:15; Heb. 1:3). He is the only way

  1. to know the Father (cf. John 1:18; 3:11)
  2. to be united with the Father (cf. John 10:1-9; 14:6; Acts 4:12; 1 Tim. 2:5; 1 John 5:10-12)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SON OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Matthew 11:28 "Come to Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:28 "Come to Me" "Come" is an ADVERB used as an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. It denotes an immediate faith response to Jesus Himself and His radical New Covenant message (i.e., Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). Notice the emphasis was on personal relationship, not on doctrinal content or ritual only. This same truth was repeated often in the Gospel of John (i.e., John 1:12; 3:16). The Gospel is

  1. a person to welcome
  2. truths about that person to believe
  3. a life like that person to live

The very fact that Jesus calls humans to respond to Him shows the need for human free will (i.e., John 1:12; 3:16). God's covenant is a combination of His sovereignty and the mandate of human appropriate response. Of course, God's initiating is crucial, but He has chosen to allow humans made in His image the dignity of responding to Him.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

"BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," AND "CALL UPON"?

▣ "all" Thank God for the NT invitation of "all," "everyone," "as many as," "whosoever"!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "weary" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. The terms "weary" and "heavy-laden" in this verse describe hard labor. They are synonymous.

▣ "heavy-laden" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE. These two terms related culturally to the heavy theological obligations of rabbinical Judaism (cf. Acts 15:10). This same idea is expressed by the Hebrew idiom "yoke" (cf. Matt. 11:29,30; Matt. 23:4; Luke 11:46). This was also used as imagery for the Oral Tradition of the Jews (Talmud), which had become such a burden that it separated mankind from God rather than bringing them to Him. Judaism had become a barrier instead of a bridge!

The New Covenant in Jesus has requirements just like the old covenant. However, they do not bring us to God and make us acceptable. They become the natural result of knowing Him in Christ. God still wants a righteous people who reflect His character to the world. I usually state the NT requirements as

  1. repentance
  2. faith
  3. obedience
  4. perseverance
  5. service
  6. daily love

▣ "I will give you rest" This is an emphatic grammatical construction. Jesus was saying, "I, myself, will lead you into rest." "Rest" did not refer to perpetual inactivity, but to a time of refreshment and training so as to move out into useful service for Christ (i.e., Ps. 46:10). This concept of a rest goes back to the seventh day rest of Genesis 1. For a good discussion of the different ways this term was used in the OT see the book of Hebrews, chapters 3 and 4.

entries.title: Matthew 11:28-30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:28-30 These verses are unique to Matthew. Matthew 11:28 affirms the doctrine of justification by grace through faith, while 11:29 affirms progressive sanctification. Justification must not be separated from sanctification. Believers are all called to Christlikeness (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; 2 Cor. 3:18; 7:1; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4; 4:13; 1 Thess. 3:13; 4:3,7; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NT HOLINESS/SANCTIFICATION

entries.title: Matthew 11:29 "learn"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:29 "learn" This is an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. It is etymologically related to the word "disciples" found in Matt. 11:1. Believers are commanded to learn and mature.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES

▣ "I am gentle and humble" These were not virtues in the Greek world, but Jesus made attitude the key. Humility and gentleness became the catch-words of the new kingdom of God.

entries.title: Matthew 11:30 "for My yoke is easy and My burden is light"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:30 "for My yoke is easy and My burden is light" There are New Covenant tasks to be performed. Faith and repentance in Jesus' name are the first step; the second is obedience and maturity; the third is perseverance (see full list at v. 28). Jesus changed the burdensome task of the Pharisees (cf. Matt. 23:4; Luke 11:46) into a life of gratitude and service in His name (cf. 1 John 5:3).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.


  1. Why did John the Baptist doubt that Jesus was the promised coming Messiah?
  2. Why did Jesus say that John the Baptist was not in the new kingdom of God?
  3. How does Matt. 11:17 apply to Jesus and John the Baptist?
  4. Will there be degrees of punishment?
  5. Does Jesus invite all men to come unto Him or just certain chosen ones?
  6. Define the terms "burden" and "yoke" in their cultural/religious setting.

entries.title: Matthew 12:1 "At that time"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:1 "At that time" Often the Gospel writers used this (and other) time designations as a way to move to a new topic or event, not a pure temporal indicator (cf. Matt. 11:25; 12:1; Luke 10:21; 13:1; Acts 7:20; 12:1; 19:23).

▣ "Jesus went through the grain fields on the Sabbath" The Talmud taught that any journey over 2,000 paces on the Sabbath was considered work and, therefore, not permitted. It is interesting that the crowds, along with the Pharisees and the Scribes, were following Jesus on the Sabbath; therefore, they also were guilty of breaking this Sabbath law. For a full discussion of the origin and theology of the Pharisees, see SPECIAL TOPIC: PHARISEES

The Gospel writers had to choose certain events and teachings from all that Jesus said and did (cf. John 20:30-31) to reveal the New Covenant and His Messianic person and work. It almost seems that these writers chose these Sabbath encounters to illustrate how Jesus confronted and dealt with the religious leaders, sects, and traditions of the Talmud. Jesus' good news was different from the legalism and ritualism of Jewish traditions (cf. Matt. 5:21-48).

▣ "Sabbath" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (NT) and SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT).

▣ "began to pick the heads of grain and eat" Normally this was legally allowed (cf. Deut. 23:25). The problem was that it occurred on the Sabbath (cf. Exod. 34:21). From the other Synoptic Gospels we learn that the disciples were hungry. Technically according to the rabbis, they were guilty of several offenses:

  1. harvesting
  2. processing
  3. preparing food on the Sabbath
  4. all of this with ceremonially unclean hands
