READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND TO MATTHEW 12:1-50

  1. Matthew 12 describes the growing opposition (cf. Matt. 11:12) by the Jewish religious leaders, particularly the Pharisees, to Jesus because of His violation of the Oral Tradition (i.e., the Talmud). There is both a Babylonian and a Palestinian Talmud. The Palestinian was never finished, so the Babylonian became the more authoritative of the two.

  2. Matthew 12 relates to Matt. 11:28-30, which describes the Oral Tradition in terms of a "burden" and a "yoke." Jesus' yoke is easy and light and brings rest, but not so the elaborate ceremonial and legal rules of the Pharisees. Jesus' yoke is not a means of acceptance but the natural result of being in fellowship with Him.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Matthew 12:3 "Have you not read what David did when he became hungry"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:3 "Have you not read what David did when he became hungry" Jesus' phrasing affirms the inspiration of the OT (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). For the historical event see 1 Samuel 21:1ff.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

entries.title: Matthew 12:4 "the house of God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:4 "the house of God" Matthew 12:4 is a historical allusion to the tabernacle (cf. Exodus 25-30) of David's younger days. But it must also refer to the later temple built by Solomon (cf. Matt. 12:6). YHWH symbolically dwelt between the wings of the cherubim over the ark of the covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: MERCY SEAT

▣
NASB  "the consecrated bread"
NKJV  "the showbread"
NRSV  "the bread of the promise"
TEV  "the bread offered to God"
NJB  "the loaves of the offering"
Peshitta  "the bread that was on the table"

This referred to "the Showbread" or "the Bread of the Presence" which was placed on the table in the Holy Place of the Tabernacle and later the temple (each weighing over 12 pounds). This seems to have symbolized YHWH's provision and care for His people, not food for YHWH! It was unleavened which linked back to the Exodus (cf. Gen. 15:12-21). They became weekly nourishment exclusively for the priests (cf. Lev. 24:5-9; Exod. 25:30). These twelve loaves were replaced every week. However, under the special conditions of 1 Samuel 21, David was allowed to eat them.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SHOW BREAD OF THE PRESENCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOOTHING AROMA

entries.title: Matthew 12:5 "the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and are innocent"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:5 "the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and are innocent" The Sabbath was a work day for the priests (cf. Num. 28:9-10). The VERB "break" is literally "treat as common." It is found only here and Acts 24:6.

entries.title: Matthew 12:6 "But I say to you that something greater than the temple is here"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:6 "But I say to you that something greater than the temple is here" Some manuscripts have the MASCULINE "someone" (cf. NKJV), but the most attested ancient reading is NEUTER, "some thing" (cf. NASB, NRSV, TEV, JB). This seems to refer to the Kingdom of God, a veiled Messianic reference (cf. Matt. 12:28, 41-42). This must have been a shocking statement to these Jews.

Jesus is greater than:

  1. the temple, Matt. 12:6
  2. Jonah, Matt. 12:41
  3. Solomon, Matt. 12:42
  4. Jacob, John 4:12
  5. John the Baptist, John 5:36
  6. Abraham, John 8:53
  7. Scripture, Matt. 5:21-48; Mark 7:18-19

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS IS GREATER THAN. . .

12: 7 "if you had known what this means" This is a SECOND CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE called "contrary to fact." A false statement is made to accentuate a false conslusion. Its inference is "If you had known (but you did not), then you would not have condemned the innocent (but you did)."

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII. C.

▣ "I desire compassion, and not a sacrifice" This is a quote from Hosea 6:6. It was an example of the preaching of the eighth century prophets, which emphasized attitude over ritual (cf. Mic. 6:6-8).

To clarify this theological issue I have included my exegetical comments from my online commentary of Hosea 6:6 (at www.freebiblecommentary.org).

"I delight in loyalty rather than sacrifice" God looks at the heart! Motive is the key (cf. Jer. 9:24)! This is one of the key theological passages in the book (cf. Hosea 8:7; 11:12). "Loyalty" is the same as Hosea 6:4, but here it is true covenant love/loyalty. Jesus used this concept in His discussion with the Pharisees in Matt. 9:13; 12:7. This does not imply that God wanted them to stop sacrificing, but to be careful to have the right motive (cf. 1 Sam. 15:22; Isa. 1:11-13; Jer. 7:21-23; Amos 5:21-24; Micah 6:6-8). For a good discussion see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 207-208, 294-295). The sacrificial system was a way to show the seriousness of the sin and the willingness of God to accept sinners into fellowship with Himself. However, when it was turned into ritual without repentance and faith, it became a farce, a barrier to a true interpersonal relationship with God."

See www.freebiblecommentary.org.

entries.title: Matthew 12:8 "For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:8 "For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath" This must have been a great shock to the Jews who had made circumcision and Sabbath keeping almost ultimate (cf. Mark 2:27). Jesus illustrates this truth in His reinterpretations of Moses and the oral traditons that interpreted and applied his words (i.e., Genesis ‒ Deuteronomy, c.f. Matt. 5:20-48). When people raise anything or anyone to the place of ultimate allegiance instead of God Himself (or His Messiah), they become idolaters.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

entries.title: Matthew 12:10 "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:10 "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath" This question is never dealt with in the OT, but the ultimacy of the Sabbath had become part of the Oral Tradition by which the rabbis of old interpreted the OT texts (i.e., healing on the Sabbath only to save a life). Their focus was on human rules (cf. Isa. 29:13), not human need!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

▣ "And a man was there whose hand was withered" From the non-canonical "Gospel of Hebrews" we learn the tradition that the man was a mason and that it was his right hand that was withered. Therefore he was unable to work.

entries.title: Matthew 12:11 "sheep"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:11 "sheep" This is one of many examples of where the Oral Tradition had become a burden instead of a joy. Sheep had become worth more than humans (cf. Matt. 10:31).

▣ "if" This is a THIRD CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which denoted potential action.

entries.title: Matthew 12:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:12 Jesus uses the question/answer format to dialog with his challengers (cf. Matt. 9:5; 12:12; 21:25; even disciples, Mark 8:17-18).

entries.title: Matthew 12:14 "the Pharisees went out and conspired against Him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:14 "the Pharisees went out and conspired against Him" From Mark 3:6 we learn that the consultation was held between the Herodians and the Pharisees, who were traditional enemies (politics and religion).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PHARISEES

SPECIAL TOPIC: HERODIANS

▣ "as to how they might destroy Him" These leaders saw themselves as Israel's defenders! It is amazing that the religious leaders saw no conflict in their premeditated murder compared to Jesus' supposed ritual and Sabbath breaking (cf. Matt. 26:4; Luke 6:11; John. 11:53).

entries.title: Matthew 12:15 "aware of this"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:15 "aware of this" It is difficult to ascertain the source of Jesus' knowledge.

  1. over heard
  2. knew the human heart
  3. informed by the Spirit

This question cannot be answered because of Jesus' unique combination of the human and the divine (i.e., incarnation).

▣ "and He healed them all" There is such power, compassion, and the fulfillment OT prophecy expressed in this phrase. Jesus cared for people, all people. It must be remembered that physical healing, even exorcism, did not automatically involve spiritual restoration or salvation.

The verses that speak of Jesus' healing ministry express the extent of it in different ways.

  1. sometimes they say "all," (cf. Matt. 8:16; 12:15; Luke 4:40; Acts 10:38)
  2. sometimes they say every "kind," not every "one" (cf. Matt. 4:23; 9:23)
  3. sometimes they say "many" not "all" (cf. Mark 1:34; 3:10; Luke 7:21)
  4. often they imply that He healed all (cf. Matt. 14:14; 15:30; 19:2; 21:14)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

entries.title: Matthew 12:16 "and warned them not to tell who He was"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:16 "and warned them not to tell who He was" This is related to the Messianic secret (esp. of Mark's Gospel). Jesus implored people not to share His miracles, but to share His message which was still in process. The gospel was not yet finished. This Messianic secret was a common theme of the Synoptics (cf. Matt. 8:4; 9:30; 17:9; Mark 1:44; 3:12; 5:43; 7:36; 8:30; 9:9; Luke 4:41; 8:56; 9:21). Jesus did not want to be known as just another itinerant healer!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

entries.title: Matthew 12:17 "Isaiah the prophet"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:17 "Isaiah the prophet" Matthew 12:18-21 is a quote from Isa. 42:1ff. It does not exactly follow the Masoretic Hebrew text or the Greek Septuagint. It clearly showed Jesus' Messianic consciousness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

entries.title: Matthew 12:18 "My Servant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:18 "My Servant"This was a special honorific title (cf. Acts 3:13) used of Moses, Joshua, and David in the OT. Because of the special poems in Isa. 42:1-9; 49:1-7; 50:4-11; 52:13-53:12, called "the Servant Songs," it took on Messianic connotations. This Messianic element climaxes in Isa. 52:13-53:12, the "Suffering Servant." The Jews of Jesus' day did not expect a suffering Messiah but a supernaturally empowered military Messiah. This explains why the Jewish leaders did not accept Jesus' message (even John the Baptist did not understand, cf. Matt. 11:3).

The Jews have always understood these Servant Songs to refer to the nation of Israel and this is surely true (cf. Isa. 41:8; 42:1,19; 43:10; 49:3-6). However these songs are individualized into one ideal righteous Israelite (cf. Isa. 52:14 (LXX), 15 (LXX); 53:1-12). Israel had failed (cf. Isa. 42:19; 53:8) in her world mission task (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6) because of continued violations of the Mosaic Covenant (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28). Therefore, instead of blessing, all the world saw was the judgment of God. Therefore, YHWH Himself had to enact a New Covenant focusing on His actions and faithfulness (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36; Jer. 31:31-34).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "My Beloved in whom My soul is well-pleased" This title was also used at the baptism and the Transfiguration of Jesus (cf. Matt. 3:17; 17:5). The Father was pleased with the ministry of the Son. This title combines the royal emphasis of Psalm 2 and the Suffering Servant of Isaiah 40-53.

The use of "soul" to describe God is imagery to express that He is a living being (cf. Heb. 10:38). This description of God in human terms is called anthropomorphism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELOVED

▣ "I will put My Spirit upon Him" Do you see the three persons of the Trinity in the quote from Isa. 42:1?

Jesus and the Spirit have a combined theological relationship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS AND THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

entries.title: Matthew 12:18,21 "He shall proclaim justice to the Gentiles. . .in His name the Gentiles will hope"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:18,21 "He shall proclaim justice to the Gentiles. . .in His name the Gentiles will hope" The statement that the Kingdom was open to the Gentile believers was shocking to the Jews (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 51:4-5; 45:22; 49:5,6; 56:6-8; 60:3; 66:18,23; see Paul's statement at Galatians 3; Eph. 2:11-3:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Matthew 12:18-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:18-21 This is a quote from Isa. 42:1-4 (but not the LXX), which is the first of the "Servant Songs" of Isaiah.

Notice the characteristics of the Coming One which are being displayed in Jesus.

  1. called
    1. My (YHWH) Servant
    2. whom I have chosen
    3. My Beloved
    4. in whom My (YHWH) Soul is well-pleased
  2. YHWH's Spirit upon Him
  3. proclaim justice to the Gentiles
  4. personal characteristics
    1. will not quarrel
    2. will not cry out
    3. will not hear His voice in the streets
  5. personal actions
    1. will not break the battered reed
    2. will not put out the smoldering wick
    3. will lead justice to victory
    4. in His name Gentiles will hope

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

entries.title: Matthew 12:19 "He will not quarrel, nor cry out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:19 "He will not quarrel, nor cry out" This described the manner of Jesus' ministry before the governmental leaders of Palestine (cf. Isa. 53:7) like Pilate and Herod.

entries.title: Matthew 12:20 "A battered reed He will not break off,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:20 "A battered reed He will not break off,

And a smoldering wick He will not put out,

Until He leads justice to victory"

This could mean

  1. Jesus treated sinners with gentleness
  2. Jesus' kingdom looked so weak and small, yet it would fill the earth with joy (cf. Matt. 13:31-32)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

entries.title: Matthew 12:21 "in His name"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:21 "in His name" See SPECIAL TOPIC: The Name of the Lord (NT).

▣ "hope" This is surprisingly the only occurrence of the word "hope" in Matthew and even here it is in an OT quote from Isa. 42:4. It does appear three times in Luke (cf. Luke 6:34; 23:8; 24:21). The word becomes an eschatological pointer in Paul's writings, who uses it nineteen times.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

entries.title: Matthew 12:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:22 This was one of the Messianic signs (cf. Isa. 29:18; 35:5; 42:7,16; Matt. 9:27-31; 12:22; 15:30; 21:14). Israel herself needed this healing ministry (cf. Isa. 6:9-10 and 42:18-22). It was a sign they refused to see!

entries.title: Matthew 12:23 "This man cannot be the Son of David, can He"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:23 "This man cannot be the Son of David, can He" In Greek, this question expected a "no" answer, but with the possibility that maybe it might be true. The term "the Son of David" was a Messianic title from 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17. It was used often by Matthew (cf. Matt. 1:1; 9:27; 12:23; 15:22; 20:30-31; 21:9,15; 22:42; also note Rev. 3:7; 5:5; 22:16).

entries.title: Matthew 12:24 "the Pharisees heard this, they said"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:24 "the Pharisees heard this, they said" This is the essence of the unpardonable sin, attributing God's work to Satan and calling that which is true, false and that which is light, darkness. The Pharisees could not deny the marvelous powers of Jesus so they attributed them to the supernatural power of the evil one (cf. Matt. 9:32-34; Mark 3:22-30, Luke 11:14-26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: UNPARDONABLE SIN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SIN UNTO DEATH

▣ "Beelzebul" This referred to the Ba'al (male Canaanite fertility god) of the City of Zebub (cf. 2 Kings 1). The Jews slightly changed the name to Ba'al of Zebul which meant " lord of the dung" or "lord of the flies." This word is spelled differently in the ancient texts. Zebul is in the Latin Vulgate and the Peshitta translations, while the term Zebub is in all the Greek manuscripts. It was a title for Satan. In later Judaism, Zebul was the chief of demons.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BEELZEBUL

entries.title: Matthew 12:25 "And knowing their thoughts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:25 "And knowing their thoughts" It is uncertain whether Jesus was using His supernatural ability to read men's thoughts or whether he saw them talking and overheard their comments (cf. Matt. 9:4). See note at Matt. 12:1.

▣ "Jesus" The oldest Greek manuscripts omit the name (i.e., P21, א, B, D, and some Old Latin, Syrian, and Coptic manuscripts). However, it is included in MSS C, L, and W, as well as many ancient church leaders' texts, such as Chrysostom, Jerome, and Augustine. Because of this the UBS4 cannot decide (i.e., "C:" rating) which is the original text.

▣
12:27
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "by whom do your sons cast them out"
NRSV  "by whom do your own exorcists cast them out"
TEV  "who gives your followers the power to drive them out"
NJB  "through whom do your own experts drive them out"
REB  "by whom do your own people drive them out"

The Jews (i.e., "your sons") practiced exorcism by magical formulas and oaths (cf. Mark 9:38; Acts 19:13). The unusual account in Matt. 12:43-45 seems to relate to this Jewish exorcism which cast out the demons, but did not replace it with faith in God, leaving a spiritual vacuum.

The NET Bible sees this phrase as referring to Jesus' disciples, to whom He gave the power of exorcism also. Thereby Jesus is not alluding to unbelieving Jewish exorcists but others who believe in Him and use His name in deliverance rites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EXORCISM

entries.title: Matthew 12:25-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:25-32 Jesus used a logical, analytical argument to show the ridiculousness of the Pharisees'claim (cf. Mark 3:23-27; Luke 11:17-22). There were four examples used:

  1. Matt. 12:25
  2. Matt. 12:27
  3. Matt. 12:28
  4. Matt. 12:29

These are a series of FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCES, which are usually assumed to be true from the author's perspective or for his literary purposes, but here they are false (Matt. 12:26 and 27). However, the FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE in Matt. 12:28 is true to reality! Context, context, context!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII. B.

entries.title: Matthew 12:28 "If. . .then the kingdom of God has come upon you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:28 "If. . .then the kingdom of God has come upon you" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE, assumed to be true by the author for his literary purposes. This is another veiled Messianic reference. It is also highly unusual for Matthew to use the phrase "the kingdom of God," which is usually found in Mark and Luke. Matthew usually used the phrase "kingdom of heaven." There are only four exceptions:

  1. this passage
  2. Matt. 19:24
  3. Matt. 21:31
  4. Matt. 21:43

Jesus asserted that His exorcisms demonstrated that His Messianic power proved the arrival of the new age of the Spirit! See a good brief discussion of "realized eschatology" in F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, p. 198. Also note his discussion of "the Kingdom," pp. 43-44. Another good brief discussion about "the Kingdom of God" is found in C. B. Caird's The Language and Imagery of the Bible, pp. 11-12,43.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

▣
NASB, NKJV  "has come upon you"
NRSV  "has come to you"
Peshitta  "has come near to you"
NJB  "has caught you unawares"
REB, TEV  "has already come upon you"
NET  "has already overtaken you"

The question is, does this phrase refer to

  1. the Kingdom's approach
  2. the Kingdom's arrival

The context supports the full but unexpected arrival of the New Age of the Spirit, the New Covenant, the Messianic Age! This surprised these hearers.

The continuing NT tension is exacerbated! The full Kingdom has arrived in Jesus, but has not been fully implemented (cf. Matt. 6:10).

entries.title: Matthew 12:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:29 This verse is often used to support the modern practice of casting Satan out of worship services. But in context this is not a "promise" text to be used for corporate exorcisms. Believers are not given the authority to bind Satan (i.e., "the strong man"). Even Michael the Archangel of Israel does not speak judgment against Satan (cf. Jude 9). The Apostles and the Seventy were given the power of exorcism over the demonic (cf. Matt. 10:1; Luke 10:17-20). However this is never listed among the gifts of the Spirit given to the Church. This parable is paralleled in Mark 3:22-27 and Luke 11:21-23.

entries.title: Matthew 12:30 "He who is not with Me is against Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:30 "He who is not with Me is against Me" A clear, radical choice must be made (cf. Mark 9:40; Luke 9:49, 50; 11:23). Jesus brings the New Age, mankind must respond to Him. Not to respond is to choose! See a good discussion in Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 466-467 (i.e., conditional covenant)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Matthew 12:31-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:31-32 This reference to blasphemy against the Spirit is often called "the unpardonable sin." From the parallel in Mark 3:28 it is obvious that "Son of Man" was not a title for Jesus in this context but a generic use of the Hebrew idiom "sons of men" or "mankind." This is supported by the parallelism of Matt. 12:31 and 32. The sin discussed was not a sin of ignorance but of willful rejection of God and His truth in the presence of great light. Many people worry about whether they have committed this sin. People who desire to know God or are afraid that they have committed this sin have not! This sin is the continuing rejection of Jesus in the presence of great light, to the point of spiritual callousness. This is similar to Heb. 6:4-6 and 10:26-31.

See a good brief discussion in F. F. Bruce's Answers to Questions, pp. 46-47.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE UNPARDONABLE SIN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

▣ "either in this age or in the age to come" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

entries.title: Matthew 12:33 "for the tree is known by its fruit"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:33 "for the tree is known by its fruit" What one does, like what one says, reveals the true self. See full note at Matt. 7:16.

entries.title: Matthew 12:34 "You brood of vipers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:34 "You brood of vipers" Jesus used His harshest language for the religious leaders of His day. In this regard He followed the preaching of John the Baptist (cf. Matt. 3:7). The Serpent of Genesis 3 could be the original source of this imagery (cf. Rev. 12:9; 20:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SERPENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVIATHAN

▣ "For the mouth speaks out of that which fills the heart" It is not what goes into a person, but what comes out, that defiles (cf. Mark 7:17-23). Humans reveal themselves by what they say. Speech is part of the image of God. Speech reveals the heart (cf. Matt. 7:116,20; Luke 6:44; James 3:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SPEECH

entries.title: Matthew 12:35
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:35 The "treasure" refers to a person's inner self (cf. Luke 6:45).

entries.title: Matthew 12:36 "they shall give an account for it in the day of judgment"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:36 "they shall give an account for it in the day of judgment" Jesus repeatedly spoke about judgment and its eternal consequences (cf. Matthew 7; 25). This relates to those who have rejected Jesus. Their lives, priorities, and words reflect their spiritual choices (cf. Matt. 12:37).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

entries.title: Matthew 12:37
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:37 See SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SPEECH

entries.title: Matthew 12:38 "scribes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:38 "scribes" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SCRIBES

▣ "we want to see a sign from You" They had heard Jesus' teachings and had seen the healings and exorcisms performed by Him, but they wanted some ultimate sign to convince them to believe on Him. This is exactly the temptation of Matt. 4:5-7 to which Jesus would not succumb. However, in reality, He had given them sign after sign but they would not or could not see (i.e., Isa. 6:9-10)!

Is spiritual blindness something God does (i.e., Pharaoh, see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD HARDENED) or must humans choose to accept or reject truth? I think this is the tension between

  1. Arminianism and Calvinism (see SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION). The tension in is an aspect of Eastern thought (see SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE [biblical paradoxes])
  2. This is the same theological issue seen in the theological debate over "unconditional covenants vs. conditional covenants" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT)

I think humans created in God's image and likeness for fellowship with Him have been given the dignity of choice. God always set the conditions of the covenant, but He demands that humans repsond in repentance and faith, both initially and continually through life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

entries.title: Matthew 12:39 "adulterous"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:39 "adulterous" Adultery became imagery for spiritual unfaithfulness (cf. Lev. 20:5; Num. 25:1; Hosea 1:2; 4:10,18; 5:3; Matt. 16:4; Mark 8:38; James 4:4).

▣ "no sign will be given" See good note in Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 467-470.

▣ "the sign of Jonah the prophet" As Jonah was in the great fish three days, Jesus was three days in the grave (Hades). We must remember that this is three days by Jewish reckoning, not three twenty-four hour periods. Any part of a day, which for them was evening to evening (cf. Genesis 1), was reckoned as a full day.

Jesus' allusion to Jonah confirms strongly the historicity of the book of Jonah. It is precisely the experience in the great fish that was used as an analogy (cf. Matt. 16:4). See my exegetical commentary on Jonah, free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org

entries.title: Matthew 12:40 "three nights"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:40 "three nights" See full note at Matt. 16:21.

▣ "in the heart of the earth" This referred to descending into Hades (cf. Matt. 11:23), the realm of the dead, the grave, or the metaphorical place of unborn children (cf. Ps. 139:15-16). This is phenomenological language: the language of observation and of common human description. The Jews, like us, buried their dead; therefore, they "lived" in the ground.

Jesus' words would not have been understood by His contemporary hearers until after His resurrection. Matthew has structured the sayings of Jesus for theological purposes, not chronological sequence (cf. Matt. 7:21-23, also could not have had meaning until a much later date).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD? II, B.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

entries.title: Matthew 12:41 "the men of Nineveh"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:41 "the men of Nineveh" This also relates to Matt. 11:20-24, as does Matt. 12:42. Nineveh repented due to Jonah's preaching and consequently was spared the wrath of God's judgment. This also implies that the Ninevites of Jonah's day were alive in an afterlife.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS IS GREATER THAN. . .

▣ "repented" See SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT) and see note at Matt. 4:17.

entries.title: Matthew 12:42 "The Queen of the south"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:42 "The Queen of the south" This was a way of referring to the Queen of Sheba (cf. 1 Kings 10:1-15), who is still alive and will appear to testify in the eschaton.

▣ "something greater than Solomon is here" This is another clear Messianic claim. It reveals Jesus' self-understanding. He saw Himself as greater than the wisest man of the ancient East (cf. 1 Kgs. 3:12; 4:19-34). See full note at Matt. 12:6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS IS GREATER THAN

entries.title: Matthew 12:43 "the unclean spirit"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:43 "the unclean spirit" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEMONIC (unclean spirits) IN THE NT.

▣ "waterless places" In the OT the desert was the haunt of the demonic (i.e., Azazel in Leviticus 16 and desert animals in Isa. 13:21; 34:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS, C.

entries.title: Matthew 12:44-45
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:44-45 This passage has three possible meanings.

  1. the Jewish exorcists performed exorcisms without personal faith, and the demonic spirit returned
  2. it is an allusion to national Israel in the sense of their rejection of idol worship, but without replacing it with a faith relationship to YHWH
  3. it referred to the preaching of John the Baptist, whom they accepted as being from God, while rejecting Jesus

The last condition was far worse than the immediate problem (cf. 2 Pet. 2:20-22).

entries.title: Matthew 12:46 "His mother and brothers were standing outside"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:46 "His mother and brothers were standing outside" Apparently they thought Jesus was working too hard or was becoming too untraditional (cf. Mark 3:20-21).

entries.title: Matthew 12:47
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:47 This verse is not included in the Greek uncial manuscripts א, B, and L or in some Old Latin, Syrian, and Coptic manuscripts. It is included in the manuscripts אc, C, and D and the Vulgate and the Diatessaron. It is also found in Mark 3:32 and Luke 8:20. It seems that

  1. scribes added it to this verse to make the three parallel. It is included in NASB, NKJV, NRSV, and TEV translations.
  2. The United Bible Societies Fourth Edition Greek New Testament translation committee believes that it was inadvertently left out of the text because of a slip of the eye (homoloteleuton) between two similar words ("speak") in the Greek text at the end of Matt. 12:46 and 47.
  3. The verse is required to make sense of the paragraph.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

entries.title: Matthew 12:50 "For whoever does the will of My Father"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:50 "For whoever does the will of My Father" The will of God is to repent and to believe on Him whom He has sent (cf. John. 6:39-40). Once one is saved, God also has a will of Christlikeness for every believer, (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; Gal. 4:19).

The NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 488, has such a good statement about Jesus' call to be a disciple.

  1. the unconditional sacrifice of one's whole life (cf. Matt. 10:37; Luke 9:59-62; 14:26-27)
  2. the unconditional sacrifice of one's life for the whole life (cf. Matt. 16:24-25; John 11:16)
  3. bound to Jesus and to do God's will (cf. Matt. 12:46-50; Mark 3:31-35)

Jesus' call to follow Him is a radical call to selflessness which demonstrates that the effects of the Fall are reversed! This is a life-long, life-inclusive call!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL (thelēma) OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES

▣ "who is in heaven" This is a recurrent circumlocution in Matthew (cf. Matt. 5:16,45; 6:1,9; 7:11,21; 10:32-33; 12:50).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "He is my brother and sister and mother" Faith in Christ supercedes earthly family ties (parallel in Mark 3:31-35). Christianity is a family based on the Fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of Jesus (cf. Rom. 8:15-17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIANITY IS CORPORATE

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why does Jesus make such an affirmation of Old Testament Law in Matthew 5:17-21 and yet reject so vehemently the Oral Tradition of the Jews?
  2. Does Jesus claim to be the Messiah in Matthew 12?
  3. Did Jesus perform these miracles in confrontation or in reaction to the Pharisees?
  4. How does Isaiah 42:1-4 describe the ministry of the Messiah?
  5. Define/explain the Pharisees'calling Jesus Beelzebub.
  6. What and where is Hades?
  7. Explain the parable in Matt. 12:43-45.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND TO MATTHEW 13:1-58

  1. One key question about this parable and Jesus' statements about a gate and a way (Matt. 7:23-27; Luke 13:22-30) is "to whom is He speaking"
    1. the Jews of Palestine
    2. the world?

      It seems to me that option #1 fits the historical and literary context best. Jesus' words to "this generation" (see list at Matt. 23, "Contextual Insights," I.) are warnings to those who heard Him speak (i.e., Matt. 15:24).
       The next major question has to do with the different responses to Jesus' preaching. There were different groups in the crowds who heard Him speak.

      1. His disciples (i.e., John 6:60-69)
      2. the curious crowd (i.e., Mark 3:7-8)
      3. those who wanted healing or exorcism (i.e., Matt. 4:23-25; Mark. 2:32-34; 3:30)
      4. the religious leaders (note Mark 3:22-30; 12:1-12; Matt. 21:33-46; Luke 20:9-19)

        The different "soils" represent these different groups. The activity of the Spirit and the spiritual ears of the hearers explain the different responses!

  2. The understanding of parables was and is related to a prior faith commitment. Even the Apostles did not initially understand Jesus' teachings (i.e., Mark 4:13,40; 6:52; 7:18; 8:17,21,33; 9:10,32). In some ways spiritual understanding is dependent upon
    1. election
    2. the illuminating power of the Spirit
    3. a willingness to repent and believe (i.e., Isa. 6:9-10; 30:6)

      Understanding involves a divine empowering and a human faith response!
      SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

  3. "Parable" is a compound word in Greek meaning "to throw alongside." Common occurrences were used to illustrate spiritual truths. However it must be remembered that to these Jewish writers this Greek word reflected the Hebrew mashal which meant "riddle" or "proverb," in wisdom literature terminology. The parables form types of literary relationships similar to the parallelism of Hebrew poetry.
    1. parables that illustrate similarity
    2. parables that illustrate contrasts
    3. parables that build to certain types of climactic statements of truth

      It is crucial to determine the type of contrast/similarity climax that the parable is intended to illustrate. To miss this is to misinterpret the parable's intended purpose. One must be willing to rethink issues and expected outcomes in light of the surprising nature of the mashal.
      SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES

  4. Some of the parables in Matthew 13 form doubles. The same central truths are repeated with different examples.
    1. The Tares and the Dragnet
    2. Mustard Seed and Leaven
    3. Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Price

      It is possible that Matt. 13:51-52 form an eighth parable.

  5. The parables of Matthew 13 are paralleled in the other Synoptic Gospels.

  6. Of the seven parables in Matthew 13, the sower/soils and the mustard seed are both in Mark and Luke, while the parable about leaven is repeated in Luke only. As Matthew gathered the teachings of Jesus into the long sermon of Matthew 5-7, so too, he gathered the parables of Jesus into one context.

  7. It is possible that Matthew structured his Gospel so that the faith response to Jesus' preaching and teaching was mixed (Matthew 8-12). Some responded but some did not. If Jesus was God's Messiah, why did not all respond? This is the question that this series of parables answers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

13:1
NASB  "on that day"
NKJV  "on the same day"
NRSV, TEV, NJB, Peshitta, REB  "that same day"

This is not meant to be a temporal marker in this context, but a transition technique. An example of it as a temporal marker is Matt. 22:23; Mark 4:35.

▣ "was sitting by the sea" Sitting was the official teaching position of a rabbi (cf. Matt. 13:2; 15:29; 24:3; 26:55; Luke 4:20; Acts 13:14). They stood to read the Scripture (cf. Luke 4:16). This position and place suggest a teaching session. The sea acted as a natural amphitheater.

entries.title: Matthew 13:2 "so He got into a boat and sat down"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:2 "so He got into a boat and sat down" A boat was usually available when Jesus taught because of the press of the crowd (cf. Luke 5:1-3; Mark 3:9).

entries.title: Matthew 13:3 "the sower went out to sow"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:3 "the sower went out to sow" One key question about this parable and Jesus' statements about a gate and a way (Matt. 7:23-27; Luke 13:22-30) is "to whom is He speaking"

  1. the Jews of Palestine
  2. the world?

It seems to me that option #1 fits the historical and literary context best. Jesus' words to "this generation" (see list at Matt. 23, "Contextual Insights," H.) are warnings to those who heard Him speak (i.e., Matt. 15:24).

The next major question has to do with the different responses to Jesus' preaching. There were different groups in the crowds who heard Him speak.

  1. His disciples (i.e., John 6:60-69)
  2. the curious crowd (i.e., Mark 3:7-8)
  3. those who wanted healing or exorcism (i.e., Matt. 4:23-25; Mark. 2:32-34; 3:30)
  4. the religious leaders (note Mark 3:22-30; 12:1-12; Matt. 21:33-46; Luke 20:9-19)

The different "soils" represent these different groups. The activity of the Spirit and the spiritual ears of the hearers explain the different responses!

This parable (Matt. 13:3-9) is extremely important because Jesus Himself interprets it. The seed, the sower, the soils, and the harvest are all significant in Jesus' interpretation of the parable (Matt. 13:18-23).

It is somewhat allegorical or at least typological. Allegory seeks a hidden, deeper level of meaning in a text. It imports meaning into the text that has no relation at all to the intended meaning of the original author or his day or even the thrust of Scripture as a whole. Typology, on the other hand, seeks to focus on the unity of the Bible, based on one divine Author and one divine Plan. Similarities in the OT pre-figure NT truths. These similarities rise naturally out of a reading of the entire Bible (cf. Rom. 15:4; 1 Cor. 10:6, 11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TYPOLOGY

entries.title: Matthew 13:4-7 "the road. . .the rocky places. . .thorns"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:4-7 "the road. . .the rocky places. . .thorns" Usually the village farmers worked together and plowed the entire field around their homes. In this larger community field were footpaths, some shallow ground and some places where thorn bushes had established themselves. All of the field had been plowed. The sowers scattered the seed indiscriminately in this large plowed field.

entries.title: Matthew 13:8 "And others fell on the good soil and yielded a crop, some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:8 "And others fell on the good soil and yielded a crop, some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty" The plants bearing of fruit, not the precise amount, is the focal point. We must be careful not to identify germination with salvation! John 8:31 says "those Jews who had believed Him," yet later in the context it is obvious they are not saved (i.e., John 8:59). The Bible differentiates between an initial emotional response and a life changing permanent discipleship. In this parable germination referred to the first, and fruit-bearing (cf. John 15) to the second.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIAN ASSURANCE

entries.title: Matthew 13:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:9 See note at Matt. 11:15.

entries.title: Matthew 13:10-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:10-13 Proper interpretation of Jesus' parables involves a faith commitment on the part of the hearer as well as the illuminating power of the Spirit (see F. F. Bruce, Answers To Questions, pp. 176-177 and Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 149-162). Parables demand a response! This response combines the power of God and the free will of the believing hearer. See introductory notes at the beginning of this chapter and also C. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible, pp. 162-167.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Matthew 13:11 "the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:11 "the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven" Jesus uses this term for the New Age (cf. Matthew 5-7) with its new way of viewing reality. These mysteries are about Him and His New Kingdom. This term is used to describe God's eternal redemptive plan that is only now being revealed by God's Messiah (cf. Luke 22:22; Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; Eph. 1:11; 1 Pet. 1:12). Every hearer does not understand (cf. Matt. 13:13,16-17,19,23; Mark 4:11-12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MYSTERY IN THE GOSPELS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Matthew 13:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:12 The Jewish leadership, with their scriptural knowledge, should have recognized and embraced Jesus and His teachings, but they did not. Therefore, those who could have/should have are more responsible (cf. Luke 12:48). Their partial knowledge results in complete judgment (similar to 2 Pet. 2:20-22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

entries.title: Matthew 13:14-15 "the prophecy of Isaiah is being fulfilled"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:14-15 "the prophecy of Isaiah is being fulfilled" This is a quote from the Septuagint (LXX), which was the translation used by the early church. This related to Isaiah's call and mission. God told him that he would speak, but the people would not hear and respond (cf. Isa. 6:9-10). This same OT passage is quoted in John. 12:40 and Acts 28:25-27. To those who have faith, God will progressively reveal more truth as they walk in the light they have, but to those without faith the Scriptures are dark and silent! Parables open truth to those who will hear but veils truth to those who refuse faith in Christ. Parables demand a response! See F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, pp. 176-177.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

▣ "heart" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEART.

entries.title: Matthew 13:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:16 Compare this with Mark 4:13.

entries.title: Matthew 13:17 "Truly"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:17 "Truly" See SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN.

▣ "many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see, and did not see it" NT believers know more of God's eternal redemptive plan and purpose for all humans than did any of the OT leaders (1 Pet. 1:10-12). This gives us an awesome responsibility!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Matthew 13:18-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:18-23 Jesus' interpretation of this parable was given to the disciples privately.

entries.title: Matthew 13:19 "the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:19 "the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart" Personal evil goes by many titles.

  1. In the parallel in Mark 4:15 he is called "Satan."
  2. In the parallel in Luke 8:12, he is called "the devil."
  3. In 2 Corinthians 4:4 he is called "the god of this world" and it describes his work among men.

It is interesting that three different Gospel authors, under inspiration, remembered Jesus' words differently. Modern interpreters must focus on the clear, central meaning of the paragraph. The differences between the Synoptic Gospels should not be over emphasized.

It is surprising that the evil one appears so often in these parables (cf. Matt. 13:25, 28, 39). Jesus asserted the presence of a personal force of evil who is out to thwart God's will for both the nations and individuals. There is a veiled reference in these parables to the three enemies of man:

  1. Satan (cf. Matt. 13:19; Eph. 2:2)
  2. the fallen world system (cf. Matt. 13:22; Eph. 2:2; James 4:4)
  3. mankind's fallen nature (cf. Eph. 2:3)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONAL EVIL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: BEELZEBUL

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIAL

entries.title: Matthew 13:20 "the man who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:20 "the man who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy" This was obviously a superficial response to Jesus and His message as the context shows. True salvation is an initial response of repentance and faith followed by an ongoing response of repentance and faith. There are many in the visible Church who use Christian words, attend Christian meetings, and read the Christian Bible, but do not have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ (cf. Matt. 7:21-23; 2 Peter 2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (NT)

entries.title: Matthew 13:21-22 "but is only temporary, and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he falls away"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:21-22 "but is only temporary, and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he falls away" Christlikeness in attitude and lifestyle is evidence of a valid profession (cf. the books of 1 John. and James). An initial response, even when exuberant, is not always permanent or valid.

The NT speaks often of those who heard having turned way.

  1. no root, Matt. 13:21; Mark 4:17; Luke 8:13
  2. fall away, Matt. 24:10
  3. do not abide, John 15:6
  4. gone astray, 1 Tim. 1:9; 6:21; 2 Tim. 2:18
  5. shipwreck, 1 Tim. 1:19
  6. fall away, 1 Tim. 4:1
  7. apostasy, 2 Thess. 2:3
  8. falling away, Heb. 3:12
  9. fall away, Heb. 6:6
  10. turn away, 2 Pet. 2:20-22

Christianity is a relationship which must be maintained! It involves an initial response (i.e., John 1:12; Rom. 4), a continuing response (James and 1 John), and a faithful conclusion (Hebrews 11)! Eternal life has observable characteristics!

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (aphistēmi)

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRIBULATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO "RECEIVE," "BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," AND "CALL UPON"?

entries.title: Matthew 13:22 "deceitfulness of wealth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:22 "deceitfulness of wealth" See SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH.

entries.title: Matthew 13:23 "it becomes unfruitful"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:23 "it becomes unfruitful" Bearing fruit is the evidence of genuine conversion and not just an emotional initial decision! Christianity is not one high moment but a life of discipleship.

Manfred T. Brauch, Abusing Scripture: the Consequences of Misreading the Bible, p. 106, has an interesting comment.

"In warning against false prophets, Jesus taught that they would be known by the fruit they bore (Mt. 7:15-16). That is, our character, our deepest values and beliefs, are ultimately revealed in the life that we live (Mt. 7:17-20; Lk. 6:43-45). Therefore, participation in the sphere of God's reign is neither guaranteed nor secured by the confession of Jesus as Lord; rather, only those who embody God's will in their lives are children of the kingdom (Mt. 7:21; Lk. 6:46-48). In his interpretation of the parable of the sower (Mt. 13:18-23; Mk. 4:13-29; Lk. 8:11-15), Jesus asserted that neither the hearing nor the receiving of 'the word of the kingdom' is sufficient. Only those who bear the fruit of its presence in their lives are revealed as those who truly grasp its deepest significance (Mt. 13:23), accept it (Mk. 4:20) and 'hold it fast in an honest and good heart' (Lk 8:15)."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NT EVIDENCE FOR ONE'S SALVATION

entries.title: Matthew 13:24-30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:24-30 The parable of the wild wheat is unique to Matthew (cf. Matt. 36-43). Here is an interesting paragraph from New International Dictionary of New Testament Theology (NIDOTTE), vol. 1, p. 299.

"The idea of the invisible church is found in Augustine, City of God; Wycliffe, De ecclesia; Luther, Preface to Revelation; Calvin, Institutes IV 1 7; and many other writers (see edition of Calvin's Institutes, ed. J. T. McNeill, 1960, II 1022). The thought that is uppermost is not to minimize the importance of church membership, but to recognize the possibility of hypocrisy and deceit. In the last analysis, those who belong to God are visible to God alone. Membership of the true church is a fact which is not visible to man. The idea recalls the statement of 2 Tim. 2:19; 'The Lord knows who are his.' It extends to the church what Paul says of Israel, that they are not all Israel who belong to Israel, but only 'the children of promise' (Rom. 9:6 f.). It recognizes the danger, which church members are warned against, of reaping corruption through sowing to the flesh (Gal. 3:7; cf. Rom. 8:12 f.). Paul recognized the need for discipline in his own life lest he should become a castaway (1 Cor. 10:27; cf. Phil. 2:12, 19). The possibility of church members falling away is one of great themes of Hebrews (cf. Heb. 2:3; 3:7-4:14; 6:1-12; 10:26-39; 12:12-28). It is also suggested by the parables of the weeds (Matt. 13:24-43) and the sheep and goats (Matt. 25:31-46) and the example of Judas (Matt. 10:4; 26:14, 25, 47 ff.; 27:3; Mk. 14:10, 43; Lk. 6:16; 22:3, 47; Jn. 13:2; 17:12; 18:22 ff.; Acts 1:17 ff., 25)."

These warnings do not jeopardize security, but give a balance to excessive confidence in an initial decision and ignores the mandate of discipleship and perseverance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ASSURANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

entries.title: Matthew 13:25 "the enemy"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:25 "the enemy" In this context the characterization refers to

  1. Satan, Luke 10:19
  2. false teachers, Matthew 7; 2 Peter 2

Anyone who distorts the gospel of the Kingdom is an enemy! Only the grace of God can help believers understand the truth (cf. Matt. 13:13,16-17,23) and resist error.

▣ "the tares" Wild wheat (darnel) and domestic wheat looked exactly alike until they bore fruit. The wild seed had a dark grain, while edible wheat had a light brown grain.

entries.title: Matthew 13:27 "Sir"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:27 "Sir" This is an example of the term kurios (Lord) used as a polite address. Remember context, context, context, not a dictionary or lexicon, determines word meaning. Dictionaries list only the way the word has been used in known literature or speech in a given language/culture.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

entries.title: Matthew 13:29 "for while you are gathering up the tares, you may uproot the wheat with them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:29 "for while you are gathering up the tares, you may uproot the wheat with them" The context seems to relate this to the religious leaders of Jesus' day. There is no way for humans to know the hearts of other humans. God will set all things straight on Judgment Day. One of Satan's most effective schemes is religion. People seem to be spiritual but they are not (i.e., Matt. 7:21-23). The wheat and tares look alike, but time reveals the difference. Many people are fooled by religiosity (cf. Isa. 29:13; Col. 2:16-23) masquerading as true spirituality (cf. Matt. 7:15-23)!

▣ "tares" This noxious weed is also knows as lolium. For a good brief source on flora and fauna, see UBS, Helps for Translators, Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 194-5, ISBN 0-8267-0021-7.

entries.title: Matthew 13:30 "gather up the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them up; but gather the wheat into my barn"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:30 "gather up the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them up; but gather the wheat into my barn" Ultimate destiny is related to what humans do with the message of Jesus Christ and the person of Jesus Christ (cf. Matt. 13:42, 50). It is interesting to note that it is Jesus who emphasizes the awesome, eternal consequences of rejecting personal faith in Himself.

It is interesting to me that there is a scriptural distinction between the saved and the lost. One has been given eternal life (i.e., John 3:16), the other destruction. There has been disagreement among Christian leaders about the destiny of the lost. I have recently become aware of two YouTube videos that address this issue. They have been thought provoking for me related to

  1. the character of God (i.e., eternal judgment has no redemptive purpose)
  2. the theological concept of limited immortality. Only God is immortal and those to whom He gives it (i.e., Adam and Eve's restricted access to the Tree of Life)

Here are the YouTube authors and titles.

  1. Edward Fudge, "The Fire That Consumes"  YouTube One Hour Lecture
  2. Steve Gregg, Hell ‒ Three Christian Views"  YouTube Lecture - 1:34:57

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT (Hell)

entries.title: Matthew 13:31-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:31-32 The parables of the mustard seed and the yeast and Matt. 13:31-33, are parallel. They are repeated in Mark 4:30-32 and Luke 13:18-19. Those who respond to the gospel seem small and insignificant, but they are part of a spiritual kingdom which will ultimately fill the earth.

The mustard seed is not the smallest seed. This is a good place to address the issue of scriptural accuracy. Western people tend to be literalists when it comes to the Bible, thinking that it is a way to express their view of the trustworthiness. But this is to miss the point of eastern literature and its many genres and idioms. It is not literalness that is crucial but the intent of the original inspired author and how the first readers would have understood it.

Several books have helped me in this area of good Bible reading.

  1. Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible for All Its Worth
  2. C. B. caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible
  3. D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic
  4. F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions
  5. For this particular issue of the size of a mustard see, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 381-382

"BIBLICAL INTERPRETATION SEMINAR"

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

GOOD BIBLE READING

entries.title: Matthew 13:32 "so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:32 "so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches" The capitalization in the NASB assumes this is a quote from Daniel (4:11-12). This would make the phrase a way of asserting how large the mustard seed plant became, here a symbol for the extent of the Messianic kingdom of the eschaton (note Ezek. 17:22-24).

entries.title: Matthew 13:33 "leaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:33 "leaven" In the OT yeast was often a symbol of evil, but here it was an obvious symbol of the pervasiveness and growth of the Kingdom of God. Be careful of attaching one definition or connotation to a word, regardless of its context. Context determines meaning!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEAVEN

▣ "hid" In context this refers to the mixing process (REB). It describes the hiddenness of the kingdom.

▣
NASB  "pecks"
NKJV, NRSV, NJB, REB, Peshitta  "measures"
TEV  "bushel"

This Greek term saton translated the Hebrew unit of measurement seah. It's exact volume is uncertain, but it was a large amount (parallel to the large tree).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES (Metrology)

entries.title: Matthew 13:35 "This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:35 "This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet" This is a quote from Ps. 78:2.

Several ancient uncial Greek manuscripts including the original copier of א and the Greek manuscripts used by Eusebius and Jerome have "through Isaiah the prophet." It has been speculated that the original text had "through Asaph" to whom Psalm 78 is attributed in the Masoretic Text. There is no Greek text, however, which has this name. An early scribe either

  1. did not recognize this Levitical temple choir leader and changed the name to "Isaiah"
  2. thought the reference from Matt. 13:14-15 somehow continued

The Jews believed that all writers of inspired Scriptures were "prophets." The vast majority of ancient Greek manuscripts do not have the name "Isaiah" in the text. The UBS4 gives its absence a "C" rating, meaning the committee could not decide which was original.

▣ "the foundation of the world" The GENETIVE PHRASE "of the world" is not found in uncial manuscripts אi1 and B, as well as some Old Latin and Syriac manuscripts and the Greek texts used by Origen and Jerome. The full phrase does occur in Matt. 25:34 (see full note there) and many uncial Greek manuscripts (i.e., אi2, א*, C, D, L, W. The UBS4 committee decided to include "Kosmou," but in brackets, with a "C" rating (i.e., difficulty in deciding).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOUNDATIONS OF THE EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: KOSMOS, #1

entries.title: Matthew 13:36-43
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:36-43 This was Jesus' interpretation of the parable of Matt. 13:24-30 given in private to the disciples.

entries.title: Matthew 13:37 "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:37 "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man" These parables relate to both Jesus as God's Messiah, who brings life and truth, and the gospel message as the content of that truth. God's truth is both a person (sower) and a message (seed).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

entries.title: Matthew 13:38 "the field is the world"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:38 "the field is the world" This is a key for understanding these parables. It is not the Church but the world (cf. Matt. 13:47). Only the parable of the sower seems to deal with those who have heard the gospel message and even then it could refer to

  1. Palestine of Jesus' day
  2. the places where the gospel was preached (i.e., the known world, cf. Matt. 28:19; Luke 24:46; Acts 1:8)

▣ "the sons of the kingdom. . .the sons of the evil one" See SPECIAL TOPIC: "SONS OF. . .", B. 1., b., 4. Acts 13:10

Notice there are only two families mentioned (i.e., Gen. 3:15). Humans are members of one of two family trees. You can tell which tree by the actions of the people! Knowing God in Christ has outward and inward characteristics (cf. Eph. 1:4; 2:10; James; and John).

entries.title: Matthew 13:39,40 "the end of the age"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:39,40 "the end of the age" This is an eschatological setting. The kingdom is both "already" but "not yet," as is judgment (cf. Matt. 12:36; 16:27; SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

entries.title: Matthew 13:39 "the devil"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:39 "the devil" See SPECIAL TOPIC: DEVIL

entries.title: Matthew 13:40 "fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:40 "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

entries.title: Matthew 13:41
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:41 This is a partial quote from Zechariah 1:3. Notice that in this verse the Kingdom is called "His kingdom" (as well as the angels called "His" angels, referring to Jesus). There are several places where the kingdom is attributed to

  1. the Son (cf. Matt. 16:28; Luke 22:30; 23:42; John 18:36; 2 Tim. 4:1,18)
  2. both the Father and the Son (cf. Matt. 13:43; Eph. 5:5; Rev. 11:15)

The kingdom of the Son is not temporal (John 18:36), but eternal (cf. Dan. 7:14; Luke 1:33; 2 Tim. 4:18; 2 Pet. 1:11). See Frank Stagg, New Testament Theology, pp. 164-165. This contradicts many premillennial theological systems!

For a good overview on this controversial issue, see

  1. SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING (chart)
  2. Steve Gregg's YouTube video, "Revelation ‒ Four Views," parts 1 and 2  YouTube Lecture - 1:34:57
  3. also a good paperback book that discusses the different views on Revelation is Four Views On the Book of Revelation, by C. Marvin Pate and Stanley N. Gundry

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

entries.title: Matthew 13:42
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:42 See note at Matt. 8:12. See SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

For a good discussion of the future abode of the unbeliever, see YouTube video by Edward Fudge, "The Fire That Consumes."  YouTube One Hour Lecture

entries.title: Matthew 13:43 "shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:43 "shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father" This was similar to the statements of Dan. 12:3. See my exegetical commentary on Daniel free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ "He who has ears, let him hear" Those whom God has allowed to understand the gospel must respond to it now! This cryptic phrase occurs many times in the NT (cf. Matt. 11:15; 13:9,43; Mark 4:9,23; Luke 8:8; 14:35; Rev. 2:7,11,29; 3:6,13,22; 13:9). These parables strike a note of urgency in the immediate need to hear, trust, and respond to Him. The response time is now!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

entries.title: Matthew 13:44 "the kingdom of heaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:44 "the kingdom of heaven" See Matt. 13:45,47,52. This phrase is equivalent to "the kingdom of God" in Mark and Luke. Matthew, in writing to the Jews, did not use God's name but a circumlocution, "heaven." This parable is unique to Matthew.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

▣ "hidden in the field" Burying valuables in the ground to protect them was a common practice in the ANE. There were no banks.

▣ "sells all. . .buys the field" This shows the radical nature of discipleship. Knowing Jesus is worth everything! The paradox is

  1. a free salvation comes by God's grace alone and is therefore absolutely free (cf. Rom. 3:24; 5:15; 6:23; Eph. 2:8-9)
  2. it costs the disciple everything (cf. Matt. 10:34-39; 13:44,46)

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES' CHARACTERISTICS

entries.title: Matthew 13:45 "pearls"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:45 "pearls" Pearls were costly in the ancient world and equally valued with gold as a medium of exchange. This phrase expresses the inestimable value of the gospel message which introduces the New Age of the Spirit. It is free, but it costs everything!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

entries.title: Matthew 13:45-46
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:45-46 The parable of the pearl of great price is unique to Matthew.

entries.title: Matthew 13:47-50
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:47-50 The parable of the dragnet is unique to Matthew. Its meaning is similar to the parable of the tares, which is that there will be an end-time separation of the believers and unbelievers (cf. Matt. 25:31-46).

entries.title: Matthew 13:48
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:48 This verse describes the end-time division of people based on their response to Jesus and the gospel (cf. Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15).

entries.title: Matthew 13:49 "at the end of the age"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:49 "at the end of the age" The Jews viewed reality as two ages: the current evil age and the age to come. They believed that God would empower a human leader to inaugurate the new age by force. From the New Testament we now know these ages have overlapped, from Incarnation at Bethlehem to the Second Coming. This verse speaks of eschatological judgment (cf. Matt. 25:31-46; Revelation 20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

entries.title: Matthew 13:50 "and will throw them into the furnace of fire; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:50 "and will throw them into the furnace of fire; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth" See Matt. 13:30, 42, 50; 8:12; 25:31ff. Jesus is the one who spoke of Hell often! See full note at v. 30.

entries.title: Matthew 13:51
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:51 It is obvious they did not yet understand, nor would they, until Jesus' post-resurrection appearance to them in the upper room (cf. John 20).

entries.title: Matthew 13:52 "every scribe who has become a disciple"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:52 "every scribe who has become a disciple" A scribe was a legal expert in the oral and written Law. A believing scribe will be able to draw truths from the Old Testament as well as see the fulfillments in Jesus' teachings (cf. Matt. 5:17-48; Rom. 4:23-24; 15:4; 1 Cor. 10:6,11; 2 Tim. 3:16). It is possible Matthew is characterizing himself!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SCRIBES

entries.title: Matthew 13:53 "parables"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:53 "parables" This was a compound word in Greek which meant "to throw alongside." Common occurrences were used to illustrate spiritual truths. However, it must be remembered that to these Jewish writers this Greek word (parabola) reflected the Hebrew mashal (BDB 605), which meant "riddle" or "proverb." One must be willing to rethink issues and expected outcomes in light of the surprising nature of the mashal. There are two paradoxical reasons given for the use of parables in Jesus' teaching ministry:

  1. to communicate clearly spiritual truths to those who exercised faith in Him
  2. to hide spiritual truths from those who do not have faith in Him

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES

entries.title: Matthew 13:54 "He came to His hometown"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:54 "He came to His hometown" A similar account is mentioned in Luke 4:16-30. There has been much discussion among commentators as to whether this is the same visit or a second visit. There are several accounts in Jesus' ministry that are very similar (cf. John. 2:13-22 versus Matt. 21:12-16; Mark 11:15-18; Luke 19:45-47, but scholars must be careful, based on their western literary presuppositions, not to assume they are the same event (i.e., there may well have been two cleansings of the temple). Luke's account may refer to another incident.

▣ "began teaching them in their synagogue" It was Jesus' habit to attend regular Sabbath worship. Jesus learned the OT during His days in the synagogue school at Nazareth. The synagogue (from Greek word "to gather") was a Jewish institution which developed during the Babylonian exile for the purpose of

  1. training children
  2. worship
  3. ministering to the Jewish community
  4. retaining the Jews' unique culture while in exile by emphasizing study of the Law and the traditions of the fathers

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYNAGOGUE

▣ "they were astonished" They were incredulous, not only by the tremendous insight of His teaching, but also by the authority of His teaching. The scribes taught in the authority of earlier famous rabbis; Jesus taught in His own authority (cf. Matt. 7:28-29).

▣ "where did this man get this wisdom and these miraculous powers" The source of Jesus' power was much debated. He was an officially untrained local boy (i.e., not a rabbinical student). The Jews even accused Him of being in league with the evil one. For them His action against the oral law was "the unpardonable sin." For those in Nazareth it was hard to believe that a local boy was the Messiah, Deity Incarnate.

entries.title: Matthew 13:55,56 "Is not this the carpenter's son"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:55,56 "Is not this the carpenter's son" There are three questions in these two verses; all three expect a "yes" answer.

Carpenter was used in the sense of craftsman. It could have referred to a craftsman of stone, metal or wood. The English term "architect" comes from this Greek term. These questions by the townspeople of Jesus' hometown imply that Jesus had a normal childhood (cf. Luke 2:40,52).

entries.title: Matthew 13:55 "His brothers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:55 "His brothers" The men listed

  1. James, who became the leader of the Jerusalem church and wrote the book of James.
  2. Joseph, he is called Jose in Mark 6:3 and a few later Greek manuscripts. We know nothing else about him.
  3. Simon, we know nothing else about him.
  4. Judas, he is also called Jude and wrote the NT book of Jude.

▣ "His brothers. . .His sisters" These are later children by Mary and Joseph (cf. Matt. 1:25; 12:46; Mark 6:3) or possibly children from Joseph's previous marriage (which is not recorded anywhere in Scripture), so option #1 is best (see F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, pp. 47 and 174).

entries.title: Matthew 13:57 "they took offense at Him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:57 "they took offense at Him" He is the rock of offense and a stone of stumbling. The stone which the builders have rejected has become the head of the corner (cf. Matt. 11:6; Isa. 8:14; 28:16; Jer. 6:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CORNERSTONE

▣ "a prophet" This was a common proverb. That which is familiar loses its significance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

entries.title: Matthew 13:58 "He did not do many miracles there"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:58 "He did not do many miracles there" God has always chosen for believers to cooperate in matters which relate to Him (covenant). It is not that Jesus could not, He chose not to. We learn from Luke 4:28-29 that they tried to kill Him because of His statements.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. List the central truthof each of these parables in your own words. Is there a unifying theme in this chapter?
  2. How does one balance a free salvation with one that costs everything?
  3. Is hell as biblical a doctrine as heaven?
  4. How was Jesus' teaching style different from the rabbis'?
  5. Why did Nazareth reject Him?

entries.title: Matthew 14:1 "At that time Herod the Tetrarch heard the news about Jesus"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:1 "At that time Herod the Tetrarch heard the news about Jesus" Matthew apparently inserted a parenthesis between Matt. 14:1-2 and Matt. 14:13 dealing with the earlier death of John the Baptist (what Jesus heard in Matt. 14:13 was not the death of John the Baptist but the report that Herod had heard about Him and thought that He was John the Baptist come back to life).

entries.title: Matthew Contextual Insights
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
